distinct.finding: A member can name itself after another member's key or its printed short form; the full key then selects the other member, and the short form makes printed commands for that member get refused.
distinct.statement: A member may sign in under a name that is another member's full 64-hex key; `--member` (and `--recipient`) then resolves that printed name to the other member, because `resolve_member` returns any parseable full key before it reads names, and the `member remove` plan and result show only the first eight key characters, which match what the person typed. The plan's letter ("a full key is taken as given", plan line 1426; companion row 312) allows this, but its stated guarantee at 2735-2736 ("nobody picks a member by naming an agent after its key") is not met at prefix length 64, so plan and code both need the change.
distinct.scenario: 1. Ana hosts G with Harbor and Maple (key K, 64 hex). 2. Eve knows K from an earlier membership (another agent of hers already in G, or any other goal shared with Maple; the ticket itself carries only the governance key, and a ticket is single-use, so she needs a fresh ticket plus prior knowledge). 3. Eve runs `goal join --name K`. `member_name` (only_you.rs:171), `Request::check` (api.rs:1046) and `JoinRequest::verify` (invite.rs:451) apply only `is_member_name` (event.rs:1011-1016: non-empty, at most 64 bytes, trimmed, no control characters), and `plan_join` (peers.rs:351-362) signs `MemberAdmitted { name: request.name }` with no person involved. 4. Ana's `goal status` prints `Member: K (9f8e7d6c) · remote · endpoint ...` because `chosen_name` prints plain ASCII alphanumerics bare (presentation.rs:235-244, 260-271, 847-850). 5. Ana pastes it: `locust --owner member remove --goal G --member K`. selectors.rs:88-90 parses K as a key and returns Maple's key without reading the member list. 6. `removal_plan` (only_you.rs:1303-1305) prints `Remove member 0a1b2c3d from "G"`, the first eight characters of what she typed and no name; she confirms. 7. The host's daemon signs `MemberRemoved` for Maple (goals.rs:548-585) and the result reads `Removed 0a1b2c3d`. Eve remains a member and keeps reading. `role give`/`role take` (roles.rs:183) and the generic `member`/`recipient` fields (mod.rs:442) resolve the same way with no plan; there the result line does print the resolved member's name afterwards.
distinct.fix: Plan and code both. Smallest root fix: in `is_member_name` (crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:1011) also refuse a name of 8 to 64 ASCII hex digits (the same test as `selectors::prefix`). That one predicate already gates every place a name is chosen or accepted: `member_name` and `add_plan` in the CLI, `Request::check` for goal create and join, `JoinRequest::verify` in `plan_join` on the host, `Header::check` on replay, and the ticket's host name; no encoding changes, and greenfield needs no migration. Reword the two CLI sentences (only_you.rs:172, 806) and the api.rs message to say a name cannot look like a key. Do NOT take the CLI-only alternative (treating a full key as one candidate beside name matches): it would let a member make another member's full key refuse as ambiguous for every agent that addresses by full key, which is a new way to stall agents; with hex-looking names refused, "a full key is taken as given" stays safe. Also print the member's name in `removal_plan` and the `Removed ...` line (use `presentation::member_label`), add a vector/unit test that a 64-hex and an 8-hex name are refused, move the `"01010101"` signed-name case in the selector test to an enrolled local name, and amend plan lines 2729-2736 and companion row 312 to state the rule.
distinct.person_sees: A stranger's agent shows up in the goal with a long string of letters and digits for a name. The host copies that string into the remove command, reads a confirmation that starts with the same eight characters, and says yes. A different, innocent member is thrown out and their agents stop; the stranger is still in the goal and still reading, while the command said the removal worked.

distinct.finding: A member's task text is printed inside quotation marks without protecting the marks, so the text can end the quotation and show its own command where the person expects Locust's command to copy.
distinct.statement: A wanted task's "title" is the task's whole text (not its first line), and the command line prints it uncut with `"` unescaped; in `goal status` it sits on the same line directly in front of the allow command, so an ordinary member's task text can close the quote and place its own command (any shell text, not only `locust`) where the reader expects the one to paste. With no hostility, every multi-line task shows in `status`, `goal status` and `details.task_title` as its entire body on one line with `\u{a}` marks.
distinct.scenario:
1. Ana hosts "Parser cleanup" (c01d55aa); the default rules let any member open a task (`propose: Selector::Members`, crates/locust-proto/src/organization.rs:155). Mallory (9f3b2c1d), an ordinary member on another computer, opens a task whose text is two lines: `Fix the parser` then `": locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member 9f3b2c1d lead; : "`. The board shows only the harmless first line as the title (views.rs:236).
2. Ana's agent Maple, at level ask, calls attempt start on it. The rules pass, the level refuses with `level_required`, and requests/mod.rs:121-126 records the task as wanted (levels.rs:260-290).
3. Ana runs `locust --owner goal status --goal c01d55aa`. `Node::abilities` (levels.rs:54-63) fills `WantedTask.title` with the whole text; presentation.rs:942 passes it through `safe` only (newline becomes `\u{a}`, `"` `;` `:` untouched); presentation.rs:950-957 prints one line:
   `  Asked to take "Fix the parser\u{a}": locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member 9f3b2c1d lead; : "": locust --owner allow --goal c01d55aa --task task:4b2d8e01 --agent codex-maple-1a2b3c4d`
   It has exactly the shape of a real line (`Asked to take "TITLE": COMMAND`). Pasting what follows the first colon runs `role give` at once (roles.rs:1 "Goal roles are immediate host acts"; `role give` has no confirm flags, only_you.rs:120; `--member` takes a key prefix, roles.rs:16-20) and the real allow command becomes arguments of `:`. The same slot takes `; curl ... | sh` or, on a goal Ana does not host, `locust --owner level ... auto`.
4. `locust --owner status` prints the same whole text uncut inside `Maple wants to take "..." in "..."` (presentation.rs:415-417, 658-664); there the real command is on its own line (750-751), so that view is a stretch/spoof problem rather than a same-line swap.
5. Benign case: the fixture text "Read and implement\nAcceptance details" (node/tests/lifecycle.rs:92) prints as `Maple wants to take "Read and implement\u{a}Acceptance details" in ...`, and access.rs:170-173 puts the whole text (up to MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, 1 MiB) into `details.task_title` of every refusal that names a task, where mockup P5-3 shows the short title.
distinct.fix: Code should change, with a one-line plan amendment. (a) Core: add one helper (e.g. `Entry::title(store, event, reader)` returning the first line of `Entry::text`) and use it in `Node::task_view` (views.rs:232-236), `Node::abilities` (levels.rs:55-58) and `Node::refused_error` (access.rs:170-173), so `WantedTask.title`, `WaitingKind::AllowTask.task_title` and `Refused.task_title` are the title the board shows. (b) Printing: make `locust_proto::api::level::quoted` (level.rs:308) the single title printer, add escaping of `\` and `"` to it (as `chosen_name` does, presentation.rs:236-253), delete the uncut `quoted` in presentation.rs:415-417 and use the shared one in `waiting_sentence` and in the `wanted_tasks` loop of `goal_status`. (c) In `goal_status` (presentation.rs:941-960) push the sentence and the command as two lines, as `status` does at 750-751; amend plan line 2028 ("a line per wanted task, with its title and its allow command") to say the command goes under the sentence. (d) Tests: change `titles_are_quoted_escaped_and_cut` (level.rs:868) to expect the escaped goal title instead of pinning `in "Say "hi""`; make node/tests/daemon.rs:258-263 assert equality with "Read and implement"; feed `every_printed_command_parses_as_printed` a wanted task whose title holds `"` and `locust ` and whose text has two lines, and assert each command line is a whole line that begins with `locust` after its indent.
distinct.person_sees: In goal status, the line that is meant to hand you the one command to allow a task can instead begin with a command another member wrote; it looks exactly like a normal line, and pasting it can give that member a role, set your agent to take tasks unasked, or run anything else in your shell. In everyday use, the "Waiting for you" list and goal status show a task's entire description squeezed onto one line with \u{a} marks instead of its short title.

distinct.finding: Binding rules that count reviews by a role makes every member a holder goal-wide, so tasks still open under earlier rules accept one holder's approval, even the author's, and their review step disappears unannounced.
distinct.statement: `rules bind` to rules with a counting role (review-panel's `reviewer`) puts every member on a goal-wide list that tasks still open under `directed` also read, and there one holder's approval is enough and the author is not excluded. So the review step the host set up on those tasks disappears, and neither the plan text nor the result says so. The code follows the roles plan (lines 2721-2727), which is silent on a role that earlier rules already use with a weaker meaning, so this is a plan gap, not a builder departure.
distinct.scenario:
1. Goal under built-in `directed`: Harbor (host's agent) holds `lead` and `reviewer`; the host gave `reviewer` to Juniper by hand; Cedar and Maple hold nothing. The lead has offered open tasks to Cedar and others.
2. Host runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation review-panel` and confirms. The kind check passes (`reviewer` is a group in both; goals.rs:162-176). `counting_role` returns `reviewer`, the active members differ from [Harbor, Juniper], so the daemon signs one `RoleHolders` record naming all four (goals.rs:239-278; chain.rs:187-198 replaces the goal-wide list).
3. The open tasks keep their round, whose binding points at the `directed` rules record (rules.rs:51-56); a new binding does not end a task round (fold.rs:875-881).
4. Honest path: Cedar's unmodified agent finishes a task the lead offered it and posts its result. `can_review` now holds for Cedar on its own result (mod.rs:437-477, author not excluded), so the result is in Cedar's own to-review list (views.rs:509-530) and the agent approves it. Hostile path: an altered Cedar needs no offer, because replay only checks `publish: members` and the current round, with the attempt optional (fold.rs:492-524); it can also approve any result already on those tasks, or a finding posted under the old `directed` binding, since the review arm has no current-context check (fold.rs:584-610).
5. Replay resolves the task's own (directed) rules with the role list at the review's anchor (fold.rs:123-140, 1167), finds Cedar a holder (rules.rs:203-206), needs one match with the author allowed (fold.rs:1181-1194), and the result is approved. The task round becomes completed on every computer (projection.rs:209-232), which also stops further offers and attempts on it (mod.rs:432-436). Before the bind this needed Harbor or Juniper.
6. What remains under built-in `directed`: the lead (Harbor) must still pick and close (fold.rs:920-940), so the pick is the only check left. A custom formation that uses a non-counting `reviewer` with no lead has no check left at all.
7. A later `role take` does not undo approvals already signed; the host has to `task revise` each open task.
distinct.fix: Plan first: Phase 4 (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md 2721-2727) should say what happens when an earlier binding already uses the counting role's name. Then code, in `Node::rules_bind` (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:239): before signing the `RoleHolders` record, walk `entry.state().rules` the way `deciding_known` does (goals.rs:316-334) and skip the automatic give when any earlier formation gives that role something one holder can do alone (a `Reviews` part naming it with count 1 and the author not excluded, or any `role_duties` other than `Review`). In that case `rules_plan` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1454-1483) prints the `--no-role` lines (missing reviewers and one `role give` per member) plus one sentence naming what the role does under the earlier rules that open tasks still follow. The CLI only fetches the current formation, so the daemon should report this in goal status beside `deciding`. Add a test binding review-panel over a directed goal with an open task, asserting a no-role member's approval of its own result there does not count. The finding's option (a), a sentence in `rules_plan` with the automatic give kept, only informs the person and does not close it; the owner should choose between the two, since option (b) makes new review-panel work wait for `role give` in this one case.
distinct.person_sees: You switch a running 'directed' goal to 'review-panel' to get stricter review. The confirmation says open tasks keep their old rules and that everyone becomes a reviewer. What it does not say is that on the tasks already open, a reviewer may approve its own result and one approval is enough. So from then on each agent's result on those tasks is marked approved by the agent that wrote it, the task shows as completed, and the only check left is the lead's pick. Taking the role back later does not undo approvals already given.

distinct.finding: After any new rules are bound, unapproved goal-wide findings and document revisions vanish from every reviewer's to-review list and counts, although reviews of them are still asked for, accepted and counted.
distinct.statement: Since 9c337df, `wants_review` (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:598-601) drops every unapproved goal-scope finding and document revision from all reviewers' `pending.to_review` and counts as soon as any new rules binding lands, although the engine still asks for, accepts and counts reviews of them and still lets them be picked. The trigger is wider than the report says: it also covers goal-scope findings, and the first `workspace init` signs a rules binding too.
distinct.scenario:
1. Peer-review goal, rules R1. Maple runs doc revise on the plan: `doc_revise` stamps context {Document(plan), R1} (requests/documents.rs:40-43). Juniper's pending lists it under "Review needed" (can_review resolves the revision's own round, goal/mod.rs:437-480).
2. The host runs `rules bind` (or the first `workspace init`, which calls Request::RulesBind when the formation has no workspace part, cli/workspace.rs:536-594). chain.rs:225 sets snapshot.rules to the new record and chain.rs:270 sets current_rules = R2.
3. Juniper's next pending: `current_context(Scope::Document(plan))` is {.., R2} (goal/mod.rs:299-306), so `wants_review` returns false at views.rs:599 and the revision is filtered out at views.rs:513. It leaves to_review, PendingCounts.to_review and the brief for every reviewer. The same happens to a goal-scope finding posted under R1, since Scope::Goal shares the arm.
4. The engine still treats the revision as live: `desired_effects` applies its round test to tasks only (flow.rs:484-491), so a member admitted after the bind still gets a host/author-signed RequestReview for it (review_templates, flow.rs:229-290) and sees a "Delivery: review request" line but no "Review needed" entry. `review record` on it signs and is effective (ReviewRecorded arm, fold.rs:585-611, calls `subject` and the reviewer test, never `active_context`); `approval` resolves the revision's own round (fold.rs:1026-1051); a Select in {Document, R1} is valid because `decision` calls `active_context` only for Workspace (fold.rs:911-913); with no R2 selection it becomes the document text (projection.rs:463-479).
5. No other list tells anyone: there is no `behind` list yet (that is Phase 8). Only `doc read` proposals and the old delivery line still mention the revision.
distinct.fix: Code should change, not the plan. In `wants_review` (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:598) move the `entry.goal.current_context(context.scope) != Some(context)` test into the `Scope::Task(_)` arm, leaving the Goal/Document/Workspace arm with the closure test only (workspace proposals are already limited to the current epoch at views.rs:495-503). Correct the two comments (views.rs:511-512 and 596-597) so they claim the round test for tasks only. Add a node test beside `results_on_a_closed_picked_or_revised_task_are_in_nobodys_review_list` (node/tests/lifecycle.rs:237): post a document revision and a goal-scope finding, run RulesBind, assert both are still in the reviewer's to_review, including a reviewer joined after the bind. Phase 8 can reintroduce the drop for agreed documents together with its `behind` notice.
distinct.person_sees: After the host changes a goal's rules, or turns on shared files for the first time, plan changes and findings that were waiting for approval drop off every agent's "Review needed" list and review count. No agent is asked again and the author is not told, so the change sits unapproved until someone happens to look at the document's proposals and reviews it by its id. Nothing is deleted and a review typed by hand still works.

distinct.finding: For an agent at level read, status offers an allow command that cannot let it take the task; running it clears the notice and leaves the agent refused with nothing shown as waiting.
distinct.statement: For an agent at level read, `locust --owner status` lists its refused task under "Waiting for you" with an allow line that cannot let it take the task; running that line prints "may take", removes the entry, and leaves the agent refused with nothing listed as waiting. `pending` at read prints the same allow line in both voices, and the plan's waiting_for paragraph ("while its level is below auto") prescribes the fault, so plan and code both need the read case.
distinct.scenario:
1. Juniper is a member at level read. It calls attempt start on an open task it is eligible for. `attempt_start` (requests/claims.rs:87-152) reaches `allowed_keeping`, which needs `start_level` = auto with no allowance (access.rs:299-304, local.rs:290-296) and refuses with YourSetting{read, auto} (access.rs:329-339). `respond` then records `Wanted` (requests/mod.rs:118-126; levels.rs:260-291). Test levels.rs:24-55 already pins exactly this at read.
2. `abilities` lists the want with no level filter (levels.rs:54-64). `waiting_for` skips only `level >= Auto` (views.rs:170-175), so read gets an AllowTask entry whose command is `allow_command` (views.rs:187-204). The CLI prints it verbatim under "Waiting for you" (presentation.rs:739-753).
3. The person runs the line. `task_allow` in cli/only_you.rs has no level check and prints `NAME may take "T" in "G" until the host revises it.` plus an Undo line (only_you.rs:423-439). The daemon writes `Allowed{round}` (levels.rs:213-219), so the want is gone and status prints "Nothing is waiting for you."
4. Juniper's next start: `start_level` is now ask, read < ask, refused again (YourSetting{read, ask}). `note_task_want` returns early because an `Allowed` for the current round exists (levels.rs:276-281). No entry appears anywhere; `goal status` also loses its "Asked to take ... at read it only reads" line because `wanted_tasks` is empty.
5. `pending` at read: every startable task falls into `ask_first` because read is below both ask and auto (views.rs:401-411), and prints "Waits for you: T / Allow this task: locust --owner allow ..." (agent voice: "X's owner can allow it: ...") before and after the allow (presentation.rs:448-466).
Two corrections to the report. (a) "Nothing tells you so" is slightly too strong: status still shows "Juniper ... · read / reads only" under the goal, and the agent's own second refusal says its owner can set it to ask. Nothing in the waiting list or the allow output says it. (b) The `pending` half predates this phase (phase 3 printed "Ask first" with the same allow line); R5 reworded it to "Waits for you" and kept the fault. Recovery is one command (`level ... ask`), after which the stored allowance takes effect (pinned at levels.rs:57-76).
distinct.fix:
Change both plan and code; the plan line is wrong, not a departure. Code, smallest set:
1. `Node::waiting_for` (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:167): when `summary.abilities.level == Level::Read`, build the entry's command from `level_command(goal, name, "ask")` under its own `WaitingKind` (sentence "NAME wants to take T in G but is set to read") instead of `allow_command`. After the person runs it the want is still `Wanted`, so the ordinary allow entry appears and then works.
2. `task_allow` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:376): when `after.level == Level::Read`, do not print the bare "may take" sentence; say the agent only reads at read and print the level line.
3. `pending_work_with_news` (views.rs:401-411): put a task in `ask_first` only when the level is ask, so `pending` at read stops printing "Waits for you / Allow this task".
4. Add the read case to `status_lists_what_waits_for_the_owner_with_a_ready_command` (node/tests/daemon.rs:213).
Plan: correct docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:3363-3367 ("while its level is below auto ... command from allow_command") to give the level line at read, and the matching row at docs/roles-and-permissions-plan-details.md:371.
distinct.person_sees: You set an agent to read. Status says it wants a task and gives you a command. You run it, Locust says the agent may take the task and that nothing is waiting for you, but the agent is still turned away. The only hint left is that status still shows the agent as "read". Setting it to ask fixes it.

distinct.finding: Starting the shared files keeps the rules' named accepting member without checking they are still in the goal; if they left, nobody can accept the first files until rules are bound again.
distinct.statement: Since a9992d8, `workspace init` keeps a formation's own named accepting member without checking that the member is still in the goal, so it can start the shared files under a member who has left; the first files are then posted, the workspace reports ready, and nobody can accept them until rules are bound again. It is real but narrow (hand-written or editor-made rules naming a non-host member by key, then that member leaving before the first init) and recoverable with one `rules bind`, so low rather than medium. The plan (roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2749-2753, details:242) still says init always writes the host's agent, which is no longer true and was not corrected in a4a5b55.
distinct.scenario: 1. Host's goal, member B admitted. No files shared yet. 2. Owner runs `locust --owner rules bind --formation-json` with `workspace:{integrator:{kind:participant,key:<B's 64 hex>},completion:...}`. Replay accepts it because B is a member at that position (chain.rs:573-581); `rules_bind` signs no workspace epoch because no tree is enabled (goals.rs:204-209). 3. B leaves or is removed. `member_remove` (goals.rs:534-585) and the `MemberRemoved` arm of replay (chain.rs:149-165) drop B from roles with a host fallback but do nothing about a member named by key; the rules stay current. 4. Owner runs `locust --owner workspace init --goal G --root ...` and says yes. `initial_policy` (workspace.rs:539-581) sees a workspace part, sets `rebind=false`, runs only `organization::inspect` (pure, no membership), and `initial_epoch` (583-601) sends only `WorkspaceEpochSet`. `workspace_epoch_set` (node/requests/workspace.rs:117-154) checks only the epoch compare-and-swap; `Verifier::workspace_epoch` (goal/workspace.rs:269-315) requires only effective rules; projection.rs:506-508 marks the tree enabled; `workspace_authority` answers Ready. The host agent's first-files proposal is recorded. 5. `workspace integrate --expected-empty` as the host's agent is refused in `Verifier::decision` (fold.rs:920-941), worded by level.rs:446-449 as "merging files needs one named member and <agent> is not it"; B is refused as not a current member (access.rs:106-112). 6. Variant with `--completion`: `rebind=true`, so `RulesBind` runs after the yes and after the capture and returns conflict "the participant that picks, closes or accepts file changes must be a member of the goal" (chain.rs:580 through commit.rs:345-364); repeating gives the same answer. Way out in both: `rules bind` with rules that name a current member or carry no files part (rules_plan then fills in the host's agent and prints "Share them again with locust --owner workspace init", only_you.rs:1375-1447), then init again.
distinct.fix: Code: in `initial_policy` (crates/locust/src/cli/workspace.rs), when `formation.workspace` is kept and its integrator is `Authority::Participant { key }`, look the key up in `status.members` (GoalStatus.members is the current-member list, already fetched at line 540). If absent, either refuse there, before the plan and the capture, in plain words that name the way out (bind rules naming a current member, or rules with no files part), or replace it with the host's agent and set `rebind = true` so the reviewed plan shows the change; the second mirrors the role rule that an emptied role falls to the host's agent (chain.rs:160-165) and asks less of the person. Do not write the host's agent unconditionally: that reintroduces R4 review finding 3, and fix-record row 3 plus docs/formations.md:102-106 make keeping a current member's part the intended behavior. Test: `init_keeps_a_formations_file_policy_and_only_overrides_explicit_completion` (crates/locust/tests/workspace.rs:615) today keeps key [0x43;32], which the stub's GoalStatus (line 184) does not list as a member, so it passes in exactly this state; add that key to the stub's members there and add the departed-member case with and without `--completion`. Plan: the code is right and the plan is stale; amend roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2749-2753 and plan-details.md:242 to say init writes the host's agent only when the formation has no workspace part and that `verify_pinned_initial_policy` compares against the pinned part as written (the amendment the R4 review asked for at its line 252). Note this closes only the init window: a named member who leaves after the files are already shared strands acceptance the same way, with no check at removal.
distinct.person_sees: Someone wrote their own rules naming one particular agent to accept file changes, and that agent later left the goal. They share the first files, say yes, and it appears to work: the files are posted and the shared workspace shows as ready. When they then try to accept the files they are told only that merging files needs one named member and their agent is not it, with no name and no hint that the fix is to bind rules again. If they had added --completion they are instead refused, after saying yes, with a sentence about the participant that picks, closes or accepts file changes needing to be a member.

distinct.finding: If new rules are bound while shared files are being started from rules that already cover them, nothing checks the rules version at the write, so the files stay pinned to the replaced rules.
distinct.statement: When the goal's current rules already carry their own `workspace` part and no tree is on, `workspace init` sends `WorkspaceEpochSet` with the rules revision it read before capturing files, and neither the CLI nor the host daemon compares that revision with the goal's current rules at the write; a `rules bind` that lands during the capture leaves the files pinned to the superseded revision while the goal is on the new one. The rebinding path is refused only because `RulesBind` carries `expected`; the new test and the stub cover that path alone.
distinct.scenario:
1. Goal G has no tree and its current rules R1 carry a `workspace` part. No built-in formation has one (crates/locust-proto/src/organization/presets.rs has none), so R1 comes from `goal create`/`rules bind --formation-json` with a workspace part (documented in docs/formations.md:96-106), or from an earlier `workspace init` that bound rules and stopped before its epoch request.
2. Terminal 1: `locust --owner workspace init --goal G --root /large --confirm ID`. `review_init` builds the fresh plan (policy = (R1, binding, formation, rebind=false)), `confirm::bound` passes, `init()` rechecks epoch/head/enabled/authority only, then starts the capture of the large tree.
3. Terminal 2, during the capture: `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation peer-review` (confirmed). `rules_plan` sees no enabled tree, so adds no workspace part; the daemon's `rules_bind` binds R2 and signs no epoch because `entry.state().workspace` is None.
4. Terminal 1 finishes the capture; `initial_epoch` skips `RulesBind` (rebind=false) and sends `WorkspaceEpochSet{expected_epoch: None, rules: R1}`. The daemon checks only `expected_epoch` and signs it. Replay accepts it (R1 is effective and before the anchor). The first files are posted and land under R1's file rule; the goal is on R2.

distinct.statement: On the host's computer, `goal status` under a formation with a counting role always ends the missing-reviewers line with "members you add or invite become reviewers." and never looks at whether members already in the goal lack the role, so after `rules bind --no-role` or `goal add --no-role` it points the host at adding people when `role give` to existing members is the step that makes results count. One detail of the report is loose: the R4 fix did change the daemon (the default bind now gives the role to everyone), so this is what is left of review finding `only_you.rs:1329` on the opt-out paths, not a fix that did nothing.
distinct.scenario:
1. Host's agent Harbor creates a peer-review goal and adds Maple and Juniper (the exact setup of crates/locust/tests/t2_flow.rs:1201-1229).
2. Host runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation review-panel --no-role` and confirms. The node skips the role record (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:239 `if !no_role`); replay creates `reviewer` as [Harbor] (goal/chain.rs:539-541). The test pins this holder list at t2_flow.rs:1270-1283. The plan and result print `2 more reviewers are needed. The role's holders stay as they are.` plus two `Give the role:` lines (cli/only_you.rs:1467-1479), once.
3. Later the host runs `locust --owner goal status --goal G`. cli/mod.rs:531-535 loads the formation and calls `presentation::goal_status`; presentation.rs:895-923 computes missing = 2 + 1 - 1 = 2, `view.hosted_here` is true, and the line is `2 more reviewers are needed; members you add or invite become reviewers.` with Maple and Juniper listed above it as members with no role.
The same line prints after `goal add --no-role` / `goal invite --no-role`, after `role take`, and (read from code, no flag involved) when an invitation issued under peer-review, which carries no role (cli/roles.rs:62-74, node/peers.rs:360 `role: invite.role.clone()`), is redeemed after the default bind to review-panel: that invited member is not a reviewer, and the sentence says invited members become reviewers.
distinct.fix: Code, plus one plan clause. When there are any, print after the count one line per such member, `Give the role: locust --owner role give --goal {goal_id} --member {selectors::member_key_prefix(&view.members, key)} {roles::quote_role(&role)}`, the same form as only_you.rs:1472-1479. Do not simply replace the add-or-invite tail as the report proposes: keep it when those members are fewer than `missing` (both steps are then needed), and drop it only when they cover the shortfall. Extend `goal_status_names_the_host_members_and_roles_and_counts_missing_reviewers` (presentation.rs:1443; its fixture has one member, so the current assertions stay true) with a second member who lacks the role, and keep `every_printed_command_parses_as_printed` passing. Add the clause to the plan's Phase 4 status sentence (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2743-2746) and note it under row 8 of research/v2-phase-r4-fixes-2026-10-06.md.
distinct.person_sees: A host who chose to pick reviewers by hand opens the goal's status page and reads that two more reviewers are needed and that people they add or invite become reviewers. The two members who could be made reviewers are already listed just above, and the command that would do it is not shown. It was shown once, when the rules were changed. Nothing is lost; results sit uncounted until the host remembers `role give`.

distinct.person_sees: If you mistype a role when inviting someone or adding your own agent, you are first asked to confirm the invitation with the wrong role name in it, and after you say yes you are told the goal has no such role and shown what you typed, but not which roles the goal does have. The same typo on role give does show the list. Nothing is lost or changed; you have to run goal status to find the right name.

distinct.finding: The watch view reads the goal's members and tasks once, before waiting, so a task opened or a member admitted during the wait prints as a bare identifier with no title or name.
distinct.statement: `watch` reads the goal's members and board once, before the first view, and renders the view after the wait with that same list, so a task opened or a member admitted during the wait prints as a bare identifier or key prefix with no title or name. Plain `wait` and `pending` read both after the daemon answers, so they print the title and name for the same state.
distinct.scenario:
1. An agent runs `locust watch --goal G`, or its owner runs `locust --owner --agent NAME watch --goal G`, with the default 30 s wait or longer. The first view prints and the command parks in `Request::Wait`.
2. During the wait a task 'Fix the parser' is opened, or a member admitted during the wait starts an attempt on a task the watcher can start. The goal's revision moves and the daemon answers `Waited(Work)`.
3. The second view prints `Ready to start: task:4b2d8e01` and `Attempting: 8d03f2b6`. `locust pending --goal G` run straight after prints `Ready to start: Fix the parser (task:4b2d8e01)` and `Attempting: Juniper (8d03f2b6)`.

One correction to the reported scenario: a bare `locust --owner watch` with no `--agent` never prints `Ready to start`, because the daemon fills `to_start` only when the caller is an agent (views.rs:403-405). The bare owner sees the same gap on the `Waits for you: task:4b2d8e01` heading and its `Attempting:` line instead.

Side effect of the same stale board: the task prefix in the printed `attempt start` and `allow` commands is cut against the old task list. Two tasks that both appear during the wait and share eight hex characters would print an ambiguous prefix. The selector refuses an ambiguous prefix (selectors.rs:46), so the command fails and never picks the wrong task.
distinct.fix: Code should change; the plan sentence can stay. In `run` in crates/locust/src/cli/watch.rs, when the wait answers `Response::Waited(WaitOutcome::Work(_))` and `--json` is off, call `super::members` and `super::board` again and build the `presentation::Reader` for the second `presentation::render` from the fresh lists, as `execute` does at cli/mod.rs:489-499. A test beside `watch_stops_observing_when_nobody_can_read_it` could have the fake daemon answer the second `Board` and `GoalStatus` with a new task and member and assert the title and name print.
distinct.person_sees: In watch, a task or a member that appeared while it was waiting shows as a bare code, without its title or name. Running pending right after shows the title and name.

distinct.finding: When the person's wording replaces a refusal of a publish step, it replaces the whole message and drops the operation identifier that had been placed in front of it.
distinct.statement: Real but smaller than claimed: with --owner and no --json, when the daemon refuses the publish step of `workspace propose --publish` (or `compose --publish`) on the rules or state side, `Failure::for_person` replaces the whole message and so drops the operation identifier that `Objects::publication` had put in front of it. The identifier is not lost for a propose: `workspace status --goal G --checkout C` lists that folder's saved operations with their identifiers, and running the same command again also works, so nothing has to be given up.
distinct.scenario:
1. Goal G's rules let only holders of a role propose files (work.publish names a role); Maple is a member without it and has a connected folder C.
2. The person runs `locust --owner --agent codex-maple workspace propose --goal G --checkout C --publish`.
3. `writable_head` passes, the files are stored (BlobPut is not gated by rules, and --owner skips the level), and `prepare_capture` stores the operation: `workspace_operation_prepare` checks membership and the folder only, never the publish rule (requests/workspace.rs:900-1014).
4. `captured_output` calls `Objects::publication`; the daemon's `workspace_submit` reaches `sign_for` (requests/workspace.rs:588), the trial replay excludes the record on Rule::Publish (goal/fold.rs:541-552), and `refused_error` answers not_eligible with a `Refused` in details (access.rs:245-258).
5. workspace.rs:1773-1777 prefixes "publication uncertain; recover exact operation OP: "; cli/mod.rs:109-111 then calls `for_person`, and failure.rs:102 overwrites the message. The person reads only `locust: not_eligible: Maple can't propose files in "G": ... (the goal's rules). The host, Harbor's owner, gives roles.`
6. The saved capture stays Prepared. `locust --owner --agent codex-maple workspace status --goal G --checkout C` prints it under "operations" with its id (workspace.rs:1205-1213), so `workspace publish --operation OP` is still possible once the role is given.
Corrections to the original: the state-side example 'workspace writes are disabled in this epoch' cannot take this path, because `writable_head` (workspace.rs:1498-1505) and `workspace_submit` (requests/workspace.rs:508-515) stop a disabled workspace earlier with a plain conflict that carries no `Refused`; and of the five `after_action` sites only `Objects::publication` can carry a `Refused` at all (prepare, connect and complete never go through `allowed`/`sign_for`).
distinct.fix: Code should change, in `Failure::for_person` (crates/locust/src/failure.rs:96-105): reword only the daemon's sentence instead of the whole message. The daemon's message is exactly `render(&refused, Voice::Agent)` (access.rs:197), so replace that substring with `render(&refused, Voice::Person)` and fall back to replacing the whole message when it is not found. That keeps whatever the command line added, needs no new field, and leaves --json alone. Add a unit test: a `Refused` failure whose message carries a prefix such as "publication uncertain; recover exact operation OP: " keeps the prefix after `for_person`. Note on the finder's fix: moving the context to a separate field printed by `Display` would drop it from --json output, because `print_failure` (cli/mod.rs:159-164) prints `error.message`, not `Display`; that branch would have to change too. Optional, same place: for a definite refusal "publication uncertain" is untrue (nothing refused is stored, access.rs:201-202); `Objects::publication` could say "not published; the capture is kept as operation OP" when the details decode as `Refused`. The plan line (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:3414-3417, "sets the message to render(.., Voice::Person)") should gain a clause that a command's own prefix is kept.
distinct.person_sees: After a refused "propose and publish" run with --owner, the refusal sentence is clear but does not mention the number of the saved capture. The capture is still saved, and `locust --owner --agent NAME workspace status --goal G --checkout C` shows its number; or they can simply run the same command again once the host gives the role. Nothing is lost; they are just not told the number where an agent or --json would be.

distinct.finding: The filter that makes hidden characters visible misses four small ranges of invisible characters, which print raw, so its own description overstates what it does.
distinct.statement: `safe` (crates/locust-proto/src/api/level.rs:567) escapes most but not all of Unicode's default-ignorable code points: U+17B4-17B5, U+FFF0-FFF8, U+1BCA0-1BCA3 and U+1D173-1D17A print raw, so its doc comment (level.rs:564-566) overstates what it does. A hostile member can use one in their own name or a task title; role names are out of scope because only the host signs them.
distinct.scenario:
1. Mallory redeems an invitation with `goal join --name $'Juniper឴'`. `is_member_name` (crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:1011) refuses only empty, over-long, outer white space and Cc controls; U+17B4 is category Mn and not white space, so the CLI check (only_you.rs:171), `Request::check` (api.rs:1046) and `JoinRequest::verify` (invite.rs:451) all pass and the host's computer signs the admission unattended.
2. `goal status` prints her through `member_label` -> `chosen_name` (crates/locust/src/cli/presentation.rs:236-252). The name is not plain ASCII, so it is wrapped in double quotes and passed to `safe`. The `matches!` list at level.rs:571-585 has no arm for U+17B4, so the character is emitted raw: the line shows `"Juniper" (9f3b2c1d)` beside the real `Juniper (8d03f2b6)`. The quotes and the different key prefix are the only visible signs; no `\u{17b4}` escape appears.
3. Copying the quoted name into `--member` reaches Mallory: `member_from_views` (crates/locust/src/cli/selectors.rs:138) compares `member.name == value` byte for byte, and only her name holds the hidden character. Typing `Juniper` by hand still reaches the real one.
4. The same holds for a task title a member writes: `quoted` (presentation.rs:415, level.rs:308) always quotes, so two titles that differ only by U+17B4 print identically apart from the task id, and `task_from_views` (selectors.rs:226) matches titles exactly.
Correction to the report: the role-name clause ("two roles can both read `reviewer`") is not reachable by a hostile ordinary member. Role names enter only through the formation, `goal invite`, `role give`/`role take` and `Body::RoleHolders`, all owner commands or governance records the host signs (event.rs:513-525, api.rs:1053-1057), and a hostile host is outside the design.
distinct.fix: Code should change, in `safe` (crates/locust-proto/src/api/level.rs:567): add `'\u{17b4}'..='\u{17b5}'`, `'\u{fff0}'..='\u{fff8}'`, `'\u{1bca0}'..='\u{1bca3}'` and `'\u{1d173}'..='\u{1d17a}'` to the `matches!` list, and add one character from each range to the `hidden` loop in `terminal_controls_and_bidi_never_reach_the_terminal` (level.rs:1046). With those four ranges the list equals the whole Default_Ignorable_Code_Point set, and the doc comment becomes true as written. No change to `is_member_name` or to the plan is needed.
distinct.person_sees: Someone you invited can pick a name, or write a task title, with a hidden character that Locust prints as nothing instead of as a visible code. Their name shows up as "Juniper" in quotes next to the real Juniper, with a different 8-character key after it, and nothing says why it is quoted or what is different. If you copy the quoted name into a command, the command acts on the newcomer, not the original. The result line still shows the key, and the printed Undo line reverses it.

distinct.finding: The level and allow commands make extra requests after the change is saved only to shorten a printed line, even when that line is discarded, and a failure there reports the saved change as failed.
distinct.statement: `level` and `allow` make one more `status` request (and `allow` one more `board` request) after the change has been written, only to shorten the identifiers in the `Undo:` line; they do so under `--json` too, where that line is discarded, and because both reads use `?` a failure there turns a change that already landed into a non-zero exit with no Undo line.
distinct.scenario: Run `locust --owner allow --goal 7f3a9c1e --task task:4b2d8e01 --agent codex-maple` (exactly the form `allow_command` prints, crates/locust-proto/src/api/level.rs:534-540). Requests in order: status (resolve_goal, selectors.rs:63, because an 8-character prefix does not parse as a GoalId), status (acting_agent, cli/mod.rs:660, because the agent is a name), board (resolve_task, selectors.rs:201), task (task_detail), goal.status (observed), task.allow, then status again (cut_goal, only_you.rs:294) and board again (cut_task, only_you.rs:311). `level` is the same minus board and task: three status reads around one level.set. The `human` string holding the Undo line is built unconditionally at only_you.rs:353-370 and 426-441; cli/mod.rs:97-101 prints only `output.result` under `--json`, so the two late reads are wasted there. If the daemon stops (or the socket breaks) after task.allow/level.set answered and before these reads, `?` at only_you.rs:365, 435 or 436 returns the connection failure and the command exits non-zero. On the re-run, `level` finds `old == level` (only_you.rs:335) and `allow` finds `visibly_allowed` (only_you.rs:389, 415-417), so `changed` is false and no Undo line prints. The daemon-stop window is a few milliseconds, so the failure is rare; the extra round trips happen every time.
distinct.fix: Code should change, in `level_set` and `task_allow` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs). Smallest change: build the `Undo:` block only when `!matches.get_flag("json")`, and make `cut_goal` and `cut_task` infallible, the way `members` and `board` in cli/mod.rs:617-637 already are (on a failed read, cut against an empty list, or better print the full identifier, which always runs as printed; an eight-character fallback can be ambiguous). That closes both the wasted reads under `--json` and the false failure. Reusing the status and board that `resolve_goal`/`resolve_task` already read is a further saving of two round trips but is not always available (a full goal id, full task id or full agent key skips those reads), so it should not be the only source. The sibling `role give`/`role take` already builds its Undo line from the view read before the write (roles.rs:249-315) and makes no request after it.
distinct.person_sees: Normally nothing, apart from a command that asks the background program a couple more questions than it needs to. In the rare case that the background program stops right after applying the change, `allow` or `level` prints an error even though the change was made, and running it again says nothing changed and no longer shows the line that would undo it.

distinct.finding: When binding rules is refused because a role would change kind, the role is named twice in the person's line, and the machine-readable message carries the command line's added prefix.
distinct.statement: When the daemon refuses `rules bind` because a role would change kind, the CLI names the role twice in human output (a `ROLE: ` prefix added by `rules_bind`'s `map_err`, and the ` Role: ROLE` tail added by `print_failure`), and under `--json` the `message` field carries the CLI's `ROLE: ` prefix instead of the daemon's message. No test or document pins or justifies either form.
distinct.scenario: 1. A goal has a group role `reviewer` (for example the default peer-review rules), so `entry.state().roles` holds it and `Node::deciding` does not. 2. The host runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation-json F --yes`, where F names `reviewer` as the role that picks. `rules_plan` makes no kind check, so the request reaches the daemon. 3. `Node::rules_bind` (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:169-176) returns `conflict` with message `this role is a group in this goal; these rules make it pick or close. Use another role name.` and details `{"role":"reviewer"}`. 4. The CLI's `map_err` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1570-1581) rewrites the message to `reviewer: this role is a group ...`. 5. `run` calls `print_failure(error.for_person(), false)`; `for_person` leaves it alone because the details are not a `Refused`; `print_failure` appends `role_details` (crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:166, 181-183). Terminal: `locust: conflict: reviewer: this role is a group in this goal; these rules make it pick or close. Use another role name. Role: reviewer`. 6. Same command with `--json`: the envelope's `error.message` is `reviewer: this role is a group ...` (mod.rs:163 prints the already-rewritten message), which is not what the daemon sent. The other kind-change sentence (`this role picks or closes ...`) behaves the same way.
distinct.fix: In `rules_bind` in crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs, delete the `.map_err(|mut error| { ... })` closure at lines 1570-1581 so the call ends in `)?;`, and drop `Value` from `use serde_json::{Value, json};` at line 17 (its only uses are lines 1575-1576; line 1716 spells `serde_json::Value` in full, so the import would otherwise be unused and fail clippy with -D warnings). `print_failure`/`role_details` already names the role for all four daemon sites and leaves the `--json` message as it came. Add a `Request::RulesBind` conflict case with `{"role": ...}` details to `a_role_refusal_names_the_role_and_the_goals_roles_for_the_person` (crates/locust/tests/cli.rs:2218) asserting the exact stderr line and, under `--json`, that `error.message` equals the daemon's message. Code changes; the plan does not.
distinct.person_sees: When a rules change is refused because it would turn a group role into the one that picks (or the reverse), the one-line refusal says the role's name twice: once in front of the sentence and once at the end ("reviewer: this role is a group ... Use another role name. Role: reviewer"). Nothing is lost or changed; it only reads oddly. A script reading the JSON answer gets a message with the role name glued on the front by the command line.

distinct.finding: One line still gives a role a duty for being the member who accepts shared-file changes, which no valid rules can name any more.
distinct.statement: One Rust line is a true leftover: `role_duties` (crates/locust-core/src/organization/roles.rs:96) still gives a role the Pick duty for being the files' accepting member, which no checked formation can name since a9992d8. The chain.rs and site parts of the finding do not hold: chain.rs has no separable dead line, and the editor code is reachable because the editor opens and keeps formations that fail the check; only its test coverage was lost.
distinct.scenario:
1. Rust, confirmed. `Validator::run` refuses a role at /workspace/integrator (validation.rs:217-220). `role_duties` has two production callers. `rules_bind` calls it at node/requests/goals.rs:167 after `checked_definition` at :161, which returns only when `inspect(...).valid`. The CLI's `duties` (cli/roles.rs:148-165) calls it on the blob of `view.current_rules`, and a binding becomes current only through `validate_binding`, which excludes any definition failing `valid_definition` (chain.rs:536-538, goal/mod.rs:44-51). So `value.integrator` is always a participant at roles.rs:96 and the call inserts nothing. No test pins the opposite: organization/tests.rs:305-321 runs presets only, and "picks results" appears only in cli/roles.rs:144.

2. chain.rs, not dead code. The loop at chain.rs:563-586 runs every authority through one match. Its participant arm is live for the workspace part (it produces "...or accepts file changes must be a member of the goal", :573-582). Only the role-arm-with-workspace-item combination cannot occur, and no line can be deleted for it; the proposed split adds code.

3. Site, reachable. `openText` (prompt/open.ts:44-56) refuses only `load`-phase and `invalid_structure` problems. `invalid_workspace_integrator` is a `definition`-phase diagnostic (contract/rules.ts:39, :247-254), so a pasted formation with `"integrator":{"kind":"role","name":"lead"}` opens and is held as an invalid document. FormationEditor.svelte:89-90 runs `inspectFormation` and `pageChecks` on whatever is held. Renaming or removing `lead` then goes through `mapRoles` (model/edit.ts:106-110), and checks.ts:130 sees `kind === 'role'`. What a9992d8 did remove is the assertions for that path in model.test.ts (the test at :488-534 now renames only around a participant integrator), so the `?? next.workspace.integrator` fallback at edit.ts:110 is untested.
distinct.fix:
Code, not plan. Delete the single line roles.rs:96 in `role_duties`, keeping the `completion(&mut duties, &value.completion, role)` line above it. Leave `validate_binding` in chain.rs as it is. Leave `mapRoles` in edit.ts and checks.ts:130 as they are.

Optional: restore two assertions in model.test.ts ('workspace policy round-trips and role edits preserve its exact authorities') showing that renaming a role an imported policy names as integrator follows the rename, and removing it keeps the reference.

Doing nothing is also defensible: Phase 9 removes `integrator` from `WorkspacePolicy` (plan lines 4416-4428), which forces all of this out.
distinct.person_sees: Nothing. No command, message or page behaves differently; this is one line of code that can no longer do anything, plus a missing test for an editor path that still works.

distinct.finding: No test runs the real program as the owner against a refusal, so neither the person's sentence nor the untouched machine-readable answer is checked end to end.
distinct.statement: The choice between the person's sentence and the daemon's is made in `run` (crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:109-112), and no test runs the binary with `--owner` against a refusal, with or without `--json`. The test the plan names for this (crates/locust/src/failure.rs:165) only calls `for_person` on a value, so both halves of its name ("only with owner", "leaves --json as it came") are unchecked. Each end is pinned separately, so I lower the severity to low.
distinct.scenario:
1. Delete the arm at crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:109-111. An `--owner` failure then falls to line 112 and prints the daemon's agent-worded sentence.

first.title: At level read, the waiting entry and the pending view print an allow line that does not let the agent take the task
first.scenario: Maple is a member at level read. Its tool calls locust_attempt_start on an open task. access.rs:299-338 refuses with level_required (level read, needs auto) and requests/mod.rs:121-126 records the task as wanted. `locust --owner status` (and Maple's own locust_status) now lists it under waiting with `locust --owner allow --goal G --task T --agent maple`, because waiting_for only skips level >= auto. first.evidence: views.rs:170-174 skips only `summary.abilities.level >= Level::Auto`, and views.rs:199-204 always builds `allow_command`. first.fix: Code and plan both change. In waiting_for, list an AllowTask entry only at level ask; at read either give no entry or give the entry the level line that the refusal itself names (the agent's message at read says `owner can set X to auto`). In presentation.rs pending, at read print the level line as goal status does. Make `allow` say that the allowance takes effect only from ask when the agent is at read. Add a read case to the daemon test and to every_printed_command_parses_as_printed.
first.person_sees: With an agent set to read, status says the agent is waiting for you and gives a command. You run it, it answers that the agent may take the task, and status then says nothing is waiting. The agent is still refused and nothing tells you that the level is the real obstacle.

second.statement: For an agent at level read, `Node::waiting_for` (and the `pending` view) prints an `allow` line that cannot let the agent take the task: an allowance only lowers the bar to ask, so running the printed line answers "may take", clears the waiting entry, and leaves the agent refused. first.title: task_title carries the whole task text, and the waiting line prints it uncut
first.scenario: A member opens a task with the text `Read and implement\nAcceptance details` (or any multi-paragraph task body, which agents write routinely). An agent at ask tries to take it. The refusal's details.task_title and the waiting entry's kind.allow_task.task_title are the full text, not the first line. `locust --owner status` prints `host wants to take "Read and implement\u{a}Acceptance details" in "A test goal"`; with a long body the whole body appears on that one line, with every newline shown as \u{a}. The person's refusal sentence shows the first 60 characters, escapes included. A hostile member can also close the quote and pad with spaces so that text looking like a `locust --owner ...` line wraps onto its own terminal row above the real command.
first.evidence: levels.rs:55-58 and access.rs:170-173 take `entry.text(&self.store, event, None)` whole, while the board's title is the first line (views.rs:232-236 `text.lines().next()`), and `allow` prints that first-line title (only_you.rs:422). presentation.rs:415-417 `quoted` applies `safe` but no cut, and it is what waiting_sentence uses (presentation.rs:658-663); goal status does the same at presentation.rs:942. The test hides it: tests/daemon.rs:258-263 asserts `task_title.starts_with("Read and implement")` against a task whose text is `Read and implement\nAcceptance details` (tests/lifecycle.rs:92). Mockups P5-1 and P5-3 show `Fix the parser`, and the plan says the entry takes the task's `title`.

Take the first line of the task text for WantedTask.title and Refused.task_title (one shared helper with task_view), and cut the title in the status waiting sentence and the goal status line as level.rs `quoted` does (60 characters with the visible mark). Change the daemon test to assert equality with the first line.
first.person_sees: Under "Waiting for you", a task with more than one line of text shows its whole body squeezed onto one line with \u{a} marks, instead of a short title. Another member's long task text can push the real command far down or imitate one.

second.statement: WantedTask.title and Refused.task_title hold the task's whole text (up to about 1 MiB), not the first line the board calls the title, and the two person-facing lines that print WantedTask.title (the "Waiting for you" sentence of `status` and the "Asked to take" line of `goal status`) pass it through `safe` with no cut. A task with more than one line of text therefore prints its entire body on one line with `\u{a}` marks, and the daemon test only asserts `starts_with`, so it does not catch it.
second.scenario: 1. Any member (an ordinary agent, no hostility needed) opens a task with text `Read and implement\nAcceptance details`; text is accepted up to MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1 MiB (authoring.rs:45, limits.rs:21). 2. A local agent at level ask calls attempt start. `refused_error` (access.rs:170-173) sets `task_title` to `entry.text(..)` whole, and the Wanted allowance makes `abilities` (levels.rs:55-58) set `WantedTask.title` to the same whole text. 3. `waiting_for` copies it unchanged into `WaitingKind::AllowTask.task_title` (views.rs:195-198). 4. `locust --owner status` renders it with presentation.rs `quoted` (415-417: quotes plus `safe`, no cut) in `waiting_sentence` (658-663), printing `  host wants to take "Read and implement\u{a}Acceptance details" in "A test goal"`; a long body appears in full on that one line. `goal status` does the same at presentation.rs:942. 5. The refusal sentence for the person is cut (level.rs:308-314 takes 60 characters, then `safe`), so it shows the first 60 characters of the body with the newline as `\u{a}`; `details.task_title` still carries the whole body to the agent. 6. Hostile variant: `safe` leaves `"` and spaces alone (level.rs:567-592; the test at level.rs:867 pins an unescaped inner quote), so a member can close the quote and pad with spaces so that text shaped like a `locust --owner ...` line wraps onto its own terminal row above the real command. The real command line itself is not altered. Note that taking the first line alone does not close step 6 (a single long line does the same); the cut does.
second.fix: Code changes; the plan stands (it says the entry takes the task's `title`, mockups P5-1/P5-3 show "Fix the parser", and plan 3550-3552 says titles reach a person "quoted and cut"). (a) Add one helper next to `task_view` in crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs, e.g. `task_title(entry, task, reader) -> Option<String>` returning the first line of the text, and call it from `task_view` (views.rs:232-236), `abilities` (levels.rs:55-58) and `refused_error` (access.rs:170-173). (b) Delete presentation.rs `quoted` (415-417; its only callers are the two in `waiting_sentence`) and use level.rs `quoted` (308-314, made `pub` as `safe` already is) there and for the title at presentation.rs:942, so the 60-character cut with the visible mark has one implementation. (c) Change crates/locust-core/src/node/tests/daemon.rs:258-263 to `assert_eq!(task_title.as_deref(), Some("Read and implement"))`, and add a presentation test with a long multi-line title. Both (a) and (b) are needed: (a) fixes the routine multi-paragraph case and the API field's meaning, (b) closes the long-single-line and imitation case.
second.person_sees: Under "Waiting for you", a task whose description has more than one line shows its whole description squeezed onto one line with odd `\u{a}` marks where the line breaks were, instead of a short title like "Fix the parser". A long description fills the screen and pushes the command you are meant to run far down, and another member could write a description that looks like a second command line above the real one. No earlier check stops it: text is limited only by the 1 MiB payload cap (authoring.rs:45, limits.rs:21), and tests/lifecycle.rs:92 opens exactly the two-line task the finding names. No test pins the opposite: daemon.rs:258-263 asserts `starts_with("Read and implement")`, which passes with the whole text; t2_flow.rs:1342 and 1359 and the presentation tests (1746, 1957) use single-line titles; `titles_are_quoted_escaped_and_cut` (level.rs:850-869) covers only the refusal render. first.title: The agent's sentence says it lacks a role when it holds the role and was refused as the author
first.scenario: The rules count reviews by the role reviewer, not the author's (the usual preset shape). Maple holds reviewer, posts a result, then calls locust_review_record on that result (or on a result that cites its own as a source; fold.rs:590-597 excludes source authors too). The daemon answers not_eligible with Rules { qualifies: role reviewer, except_author: true }. The tool's message reads `codex-maple can't approve this result in this goal: approving needs a role codex-maple does not hold and codex-maple may be its author (the goal's rules). The host gives roles.` Maple does hold the role. With --owner the person reads `approving needs a reviewer other than the author and Maple is not one ... The host, Harbor's owner, gives roles.`
first.evidence: level.rs:417-424 always writes `a role {who} does not hold` for a role selector in the agent's voice and only appends the hedge `may be its author`. level.rs:258-267 then always adds `The host gives roles.` whenever the selector names a role. Refused carries neither whether the agent holds the role nor whether it is the author, so render cannot tell the two cases apart. The plan's fixed phrase (`a role WHO does not hold`, plan line 3290-3291) and mockup P5-2 line 3 cover only the case without except_author.
first.fix: Code and plan both change. For a role rule with except_author, do not assert that the agent lacks the role: say what the rule asks (`approving needs a role, held by someone other than the result's author`) and end with `pick other work` rather than sending the reader to the host, or add to Why::Rules whether the agent holds the role so each case gets a true sentence. Pin the author case in each_side_reads_as_one_sentence_in_both_voices.
first.person_sees: An agent that is a reviewer and tries to approve its own result is told it does not hold a needed role and that the host gives roles. It, or its owner, may then ask the host for a role it already has.

second.statement: When a rule counts reviews by a role and excludes the author, the agent-voice refusal always asserts "a role WHO does not hold" and ends "The host gives roles.", even when the agent holds the role and was refused only because it wrote the result (or one of its sources). The person-voice sentence stays literally true but ends with the same pointer to the host, which cannot help.
second.scenario:

The tool returns: `codex-maple can't approve this result in this goal: approving needs a role codex-maple does not hold and codex-maple may be its author (the goal's rules). The host gives roles.` With --owner the person reads `approving needs a reviewer other than the author and Maple is not one (the goal's rules). The host, Harbor's owner, gives roles.`

Code and plan both change; the code follows the plan's fixed phrase literally and the plan has no wording for the author case.

first.title: A role clash on rules bind names the role twice, and its --json message is rewritten by the command line
first.scenario: The person hosts a goal where `lead` picks or closes, and binds rules that make `lead` a group: `locust --owner rules bind --goal G ...`. The daemon answers conflict with details {"role":"lead"}. The person reads `locust: conflict: lead: this role picks or closes in this goal and has one holder; these rules make it a group. Use another role name. Role: lead`. With --json, error.message is `lead: this role picks ...`, which is not the daemon's message.
first.evidence: Two sessions each answered review finding goals.rs:170. only_you.rs:1570-1581 (commit ec1e078) prefixes the role to `error.message` for a conflict whose details carry `role`, with no check of --json. cli/mod.rs:172-195 `role_details` (commit 9c337df) appends ` Role: X` for any failure whose details carry `role`. Both run for the same error (daemon site goals.rs:176). No test pins the combined line; cli.rs:2218-2269 covers only the role give case. Plan line 3405-3406: 'Under --json the daemon's message and details are printed as they came'.
first.fix: Code should change: remove the `map_err` at only_you.rs:1570-1581 and let `role_details` name the role, which the review asked to be the one place. Add the rules-bind clash to the cli.rs test.
first.person_sees: The refusal repeats the role name at the start and the end of the same line. Scripts reading --json get a message that the command line altered.

second.statement: A role-kind clash on `rules bind` is named twice in the human line (prefix `lead: ` from only_you.rs and suffix ` Role: lead` from `role_details`), and the prefix is also written into `error.message` under `--json`, where the role is already in `details`. Cosmetic only; nothing is lost or changed, and no test pins the combined line.
second.scenario: 1. The person hosts a goal whose current or past rules make `lead` a deciding role (picks or closes). 2. They run `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation-json F`, where F still declares `lead` with duties but only as a group (for example named only in a review selector). `rules_plan` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1354-1505) makes no kind check, so the plan prints and they answer yes. 3. The daemon's `rules_bind` (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:163-177) answers `conflict` with message "this role picks or closes in this goal and has one holder; these rules make it a group. Use another role name." and details {"role":"lead"}. 4. The `map_err` at only_you.rs:1570-1581 rewrites the message to "lead: this role picks ...", with no check of --json. 5. `execute` returns the error; `for_person` leaves it alone because the details are not a `Refused` (failure.rs:200-204); `print_failure` (cli/mod.rs:159-169) prints `locust: {error}{role_details}`, so stderr reads `locust: conflict: lead: this role picks or closes in this goal and has one holder; these rules make it a group. Use another role name. Role: lead`. With --json, stdout carries error.message "lead: this role picks ..." beside details {"role":"lead"}.
second.fix: Code should change: in `rules_bind` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1570-1581) delete the `.map_err` that prefixes the role onto `error.message`, leaving `role_details` in crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:172-195 as the one place that names the role (the R4 review's "one place" fix, whose own example was `... Use another role name. Role: lead`). Extend the stub test `a_role_refusal_names_the_role_and_the_goals_roles_for_the_person` in crates/locust/tests/cli.rs (or add a sibling) with a `Request::RulesBind` that returns `conflict` with details {"role":"lead"}, pinning the human line and that the --json message equals the daemon's.
second.person_sees: After saying yes to a rules change that clashes with an existing role, the refusal names the role at both ends of one line: "lead: this role picks or closes ... Use another role name. Role: lead". It still tells them which role and what to do, so nothing is lost; it just reads as a stutter. A script reading --json gets the role name glued to the front of the message as well as in the details field.
second.reason: Read both sites at HEAD (a4a5b55 changes docs only since 9c337df). only_you.rs:1570-1581 (blame: ec1e078) sets `error.message = format!("{}: {}", safe(role), error.message)` for any Conflict whose details carry a string `role`, unconditionally of --json. cli/mod.rs:166 and 172-195 (blame: 9c337df) append ` Role: X` in human mode for any failure whose details carry `role`. The only daemon conflict carrying `role` on this request is goals.rs:176, and details survive the trip (connection.rs:34 `ClientError::Api(error) => error.into()`, failure.rs:117-122). Nothing earlier stops it: `rules_plan` has no deciding/kind check (grep for `deciding` in only_you.rs finds only a test fixture at 1866), and `for_person` does not touch non-Refused details (failure.rs:200-204). No test pins either outcome: `git grep` for the clash sentence finds only goals.rs:172/174, and cli.rs:2218-2269 stubs only `RoleGive`. Nothing declares the double naming intended: the R5 build notes (research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md:51-56) describe only the `Role:` suffix as the answer to review finding goals.rs:170, the R4 fix record does not mention the prefix at all, and the R4 review (research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:614) asked for one place in `print_failure`. Severity stays low. The workspace-init path that also sends RulesBind does not pass through this map_err, so it prints the role once; removing the map_err makes both paths agree.

first.title: At level read, "Waiting for you" and pending print an allow line that does not let the agent take the task
first.scenario: Juniper is a member of "Parser cleanup" at level read (the state mockup P5-1 shows). Juniper calls locust_attempt_start on task T and is refused level_required (level read, needs auto); the want is noted. `locust --owner status` prints "Waiting for you / Juniper wants to take "T" in "Parser cleanup" / locust --owner allow --goal c01d55aa --task task:... --agent claude-juniper-77aa0c52". The person runs the line as printed. It answers "claude-juniper-77aa0c52 may take "T" in "Parser cleanup" until the host revises it." with an Undo line. Juniper starts again and is refused again (level read, needs ask). The want has become an allowance, so no new want is noted and status now says "Nothing is waiting for you." The same happens from `pending`: at read every startable task is listed as "Waits for you: T / Allow this task: locust --owner allow ...". Expected: at read the entry carries the line that actually helps (`level ... ask`), or says both steps.

An allowance only lowers the start threshold to ask (local.rs:289-296), and access.rs:329-339 refuses when level < needed, so read stays refused. note_task_want returns early when a current-round allowance exists (requests/levels.rs:276-281), so the entry never comes back. pending puts every task in ask_first when level < start_level (views.rs:401-411) and prints the allow line for it (presentation.rs:452-468). Goal status already handles this case: presentation.rs:943-948, comment "An allowance lowers the bar to ask, so at read only a level helps", prints level_command there. The plan has the same gap ("while its level is below auto", plan lines 3351-3356) while its Goal says each line carries the command that settles it. The test status_lists_what_waits_for_the_owner_with_a_ready_command only runs at Level::Ask.
first.fix: Change code and plan. In waiting_for, at Level::Read give the `locust --owner level --goal G --agent NAME ask` line (level_command) with a sentence that says the agent is at read, as goal status does; do the same for ask_first in pending; make the `allow` answer at read say the agent must also be at ask (only_you.rs:428). Reword plan lines 3351-3356 to say what an agent at read gets. Add a read case to the daemon test.
first.person_sees: With an agent set to read, status says the agent wants a task and prints an allow command. You run it, Locust says the agent may take the task, and status then says nothing is waiting. The agent is still refused, and nothing on screen tells you that you also have to raise its level.

second.statement: Confirmed as written, at medium rather than high severity. For an agent at level read, `status` ("Waiting for you") and `pending` print an `allow` line that cannot let the agent take the task; `allow` answers "may take", the want is consumed, and status then says nothing is waiting while the agent is still refused. The code follows the plan's "below auto" wording, so plan and code both need the change.
second.scenario: 1. Juniper is a member at level read (set with `level ... read` or `--level read` at join). 2. Juniper calls locust_attempt_start on task T: access.rs:299-303 sets needed = start_level = auto (local.rs:290-296, no allowance), access.rs:329-339 refuses level_required {level read, needs auto}; requests/mod.rs:120-126 calls note_task_want, which stores Allowance::Wanted (pinned at read by tests/levels.rs:25-55). 3. `locust --owner status`: waiting_for (views.rs:167-209) skips only level >= auto, so it emits AllowTask with allow_command; presentation.rs:646-664 and 744-753 print "Juniper wants to take "T" in "G"" over `locust --owner allow --goal .. --task .. --agent ..`. 4. The person runs it: task_allow (requests/levels.rs:179-230) has no level check and writes Allowed; only_you.rs:423-428 prints "NAME may take "T" in "G" until the host revises it." plus an Undo line. 5. Juniper retries: start_level is now ask, read < ask, refused level_required {read, needs ask}. note_task_want returns early because an Allowed for the current round exists (requests/levels.rs:276-281), and abilities() lists it under allowed_tasks, not wanted_tasks, so status prints "Nothing is waiting for you." 6. Separately, `pending` at read puts every startable task in ask_first (views.rs:401-411) and prints "Waits for you: T / Allow this task: locust --owner allow ..." (presentation.rs:452-468); the agent's own view says "<owner> can allow it: ...". Corrections to the report: the level is still on screen under the goal ("Juniper · member · read / reads only; ..."), and the agent's second refusal does name the right fix ("owner can set X to ask"), after which the stored allowance works; so recovery is one more command, with nothing lost. second.fix: Change code and plan. Code: (a) Node::waiting_for (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:167): when summary.abilities.level == Level::Read, build `command` with level_command(goal, name, "ask") instead of allow_command, and carry that fact in the entry (a second WaitingKind variant or a level field) so waiting_sentence (crates/locust/src/cli/presentation.rs:646) can say "but at read it only reads", as goal_status already does at presentation.rs:943-948. (b) task_allow in crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:423-428: when after.level == Level::Read, do not say "may take"; say the agent must also be at ask and print the level line.
