first.title: Two members with the same name still cannot be told apart by who joined first (second half of the name finding is not built)
first.scenario: Goal "Parser cleanup" under directed, members Maple (host's agent) and Juniper, one invitation still open. The invitee joins with --name Juniper (same bytes); the host's computer admits it unattended. The host's `goal status` prints two lines "Member: Juniper (51c2e9aa) ..." and "Member: Juniper (9f3b2c1d) ..." in key order. `role give --member Juniper lead` answers "member selector Juniper is ambiguous; choose a key prefix: Juniper (51c2e9aa), Juniper (9f3b2c1d)", also in key order. Nothing says which Juniper is the newcomer, so the host picks a prefix by guess and can give lead to the newcomer. Expected, per the review: members print in join order (the host-signed admission position) and the later one is marked in the refusal.
first.evidence: MemberView has no admission position (api.rs:1538-1546); goal_status prints view.members as given (presentation.rs:847-858); the ambiguous-selector refusal lists candidates from a BTreeSet of keys with no mark (selectors.rs:136-173). Build notes departure 8 (lines 173-182) declares the join order, the ordered list and the "later" mark as not built, while the commit message says the findings assigned to this phase are fixed. The parts that are done: safe now escapes the default-ignorable code points (level.rs:567-594) and chosen_name quotes any name that is not plain ASCII (presentation.rs:236-252), so a hidden character or a look-alike letter prints differently from the original. The exact-duplicate case is unchanged.
first.fix: Change code and plan, as the review's fix says: add the admission position to MemberView in goal_status (node/requests/goals.rs), print members in that order in presentation::goal_status, mark the later holder in the ambiguous-selector refusal (selectors.rs:155), and add the sentence to the plan's member_label paragraph. Both files are free now that the fix session has landed.
first.person_sees: Someone you invited can join under the same name as an existing member. Goal status then shows two lines with that name and different 8-character keys, and nothing says which one joined later. Picking the wrong key gives a role to the newcomer.

second.statement: The join-order half of the R4 review's name finding (event.rs:1011, second entry) is not built: `MemberView` carries no admission position, `goal status` and the shared-name refusal list members in key order, and nothing marks which of two identically named members joined later. The hidden-character and look-alike half is done; the exact-duplicate case is unchanged, and neither the plan nor any later phase now owns the rest, although commit 9c337df says the findings assigned to the phase are fixed.
second.scenario:
1. Goal "Parser cleanup" under directed; members Maple (host's agent) and Juniper (remote); one invitation still open.
2. The invitee runs `goal join --name Juniper`. `plan_join` (crates/locust-core/src/node/peers.rs:344-364) checks only that the key is not already a member and signs `MemberAdmitted` with that name, with no person involved.
3. On the host, `goal status` prints two `Member: Juniper (<8 hex>) · remote · endpoint <8 hex>` lines. Their order is the `BTreeMap<PublicKey, Member>` iteration order (state.rs:208, goals.rs:455-465), so it is key order, not join order.
4. `role give --member Juniper lead` and also `member remove --member Juniper` (only_you.rs:1322) both go through `resolve_member` -> `member_from_views` and stop with "member selector Juniper is ambiguous; choose a key prefix: Juniper (51c2e9aa), Juniper (9f3b2c1d)", candidates from a `BTreeSet` of keys, no mark.
5. The host has to pick a prefix with nothing in any plain view saying which one is the newcomer. `goal invitations` prints the redeeming key per ticket but no time or order. A wrong pick gives lead to the newcomer (the result's holders line shows the key and an Undo is printed) or removes the original member.
second.fix: Change code and plan together, as the review's fix 1 says. In `goal_status` (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:455) add the admission's position on the host's chain to `MemberView` (from `Member.admission` through the chain's `position`, chain.rs:289) and emit `members` sorted by it, so `presentation::goal_status` prints join order as given. In `member_from_views` (crates/locust/src/cli/selectors.rs:132) keep candidates in that order instead of a key-ordered `BTreeSet` and mark every candidate after the first as joined later; that covers `role give`, `member remove` and the generic `--member`/`--recipient` path at once. Update the pinned strings in `a_member_resolves_by_key_prefix_then_name_and_a_shared_name_lists_key_prefixes`, regenerate runtime.contract.json, and add the sentence to the plan's `member_label`/`resolve_member` paragraph (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md about line 2729-2740) and the companion row at details line 312. Also correct build-notes departure 8 or the commit claim so the item has an owner.
second.person_sees: Someone you invited can join under exactly the same name as a member you already have. Goal status then shows two lines with that name and two different 8-character keys, and when you try to give a role to, or remove, that name, the command stops and asks you to pick a key, but nothing tells you which one joined later. If you pick the wrong key, the newcomer gets the role (the printed Undo line puts it back), or the member you meant to keep is removed.
second.reason: I tried to break each step and could not. Reachable: `plan_join` never compares names (peers.rs:344-364), and no fix commit added such a check (2de65f0 touched peers.rs only for the retry path). No position in the view: `MemberView` is name, member, endpoint, local only (crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:1538-1546); `goal_status` fills it by iterating `state.members`, a `BTreeMap<PublicKey, Member>` (state.rs:208; goals.rs:455-465), although `Member.admission` (state.rs:17) and `chain.position` (chain.rs:289) exist to supply it. Printing: `presentation::goal_status` loops `view.members` as given (presentation.rs:847-858) and `member_label_noting` adds only the 8-character prefix (presentation.rs:260-272). Refusal: `member_from_views` collects a `BTreeSet` of keys and prints `name (prefix)` with no mark (selectors.rs:132-173); its test pins `Maple (01010101), Maple (02020202)` (selectors.rs:383-389), which is silent on join order rather than a decision against it. Not intended: the review's fix 1 asks for exactly this and assigns it to R5 (research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:347-358); the builder's notes departure 8 says it was not built because the two files were being rewritten by the concurrent session (research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md:173-182), a deferral with no later owner; the R4 fix record does not list the finding at all; the plan has no join-order sentence (grep of docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md, including a4a5b55's fold-in). The done half checks out: `safe` escapes the default-ignorable ranges (crates/locust-proto/src/api/level.rs:567-594), `chosen_name` quotes anything outside plain ASCII (presentation.rs:236-252), and the `is_member_name` comment was corrected in 2de65f0. Severity stays medium: keys always differ, the tool refuses rather than picking, and role changes print an Undo, but the same refusal also fronts `member remove` (only_you.rs:1322), where a wrong guess is not undone by a printed line, and the only other hint, `goal invitations`, prints the redeeming key without order (crates/locust/src/cli/invitations.rs:181-197).

first.title: A reviewer refused because it wrote the result is told it lacks a role and that the host gives roles
first.scenario: review-panel goal: a result counts with approvals from the role reviewer, not the author's. Maple holds reviewer (every invited member gets it by default). Maple calls locust_review_record on its own result, or on a result that names Maple's earlier result as a source. The engine refuses with the rule's selector Role{reviewer} and except_author = true; the refusal does not say which of the two tests failed. The tool's message is "codex-maple-1a2b3c4d can't approve this result in this goal: approving needs a role codex-maple-1a2b3c4d does not hold and codex-maple-1a2b3c4d may be its author (the goal's rules). The host gives roles." Maple does hold the role. With --owner --agent the person reads "... approving needs a reviewer other than the author and Maple is not one (the goal's rules). The host, Harbor's owner, gives roles.", which sends them to the host for a role Maple already has.
first.evidence: fold.rs:590-611 refuses through may_review_with_authors (author and source authors) and records only (Rule::Review, qualifies, except_author). rule_sentence writes "a role {who} does not hold" for every Role selector in the agent's voice and only appends "{who} may be its author" (level.rs:417-424); render then closes with "The host gives roles." whenever the selector names a role (level.rs:258-267). The build notes (departure 2) say these sentences were inferred from mockup P5-2, which has no author-excluded case. rules_and_state_never_suggest_a_level runs this combination but only checks that the words level, allow and locust are absent.
first.fix: Change code, and add the author-excluded sentence to the plan. Either carry in Why::Rules whether the agent holds a named role (the daemon has state().roles when it builds the refusal in access.rs:252-258) and word the two cases apart, or use a sentence true in both, such as "approving needs a role, held by a member other than the result's author", and end with "Nothing to change; pick other work." unless the agent lacks the role. Add a level.rs test for a holder who is the author.
first.person_sees: An agent that already is a reviewer and tries to approve its own work is told it needs a role it does not have and that the host gives roles. It may then ask you, and you the host, for a role it already holds.

second.statement: When a goal's review rule is "role R, not the author" and a member who holds R tries to approve its own result (or a file proposal that lists its result as a source), the agent's refusal sentence flatly says it lacks a role it holds, and both voices close with "The host gives roles", a remedy that cannot help. Under review-panel every added or invited member is a reviewer by default, so authorship is the usual way a member meets this refusal there.
second.scenario:
1. Goal on the review-panel preset: completion is Reviews{by: role reviewer, count 2, exclude_author: true} (crates/locust-proto/src/organization/presets.rs:69-79). Maple was added or invited without --no-role, so it holds reviewer (crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:63-75, goals.rs:239).
2. Maple posts a result, then calls locust_review_record on it (or on a workspace proposal whose sources include Maple's proposal). Request::ReviewRecord -> review_record (node/requests/tasks.rs:226-251) -> sign_for -> allowed_keeping; nothing earlier stops it (subject_context only looks the result up).
3. Replay refuses at goal/fold.rs:590-611: may_review_with_authors is false because source_authors contains Maple (rules.rs:291-309, workspace.rs:361-381). The refusal recorded is (Rule::Review, Role{reviewer}, except_author=true); it does not say which test failed.
4. access.rs:249-258 turns it into Why::Rules; the rules refusal comes before the level check and before the owner_act shortcut, so both an agent and a person's --owner --agent command get it.
5. Agent's message (level.rs:416-424, 258-267): "codex-maple-1a2b3c4d can't approve this result in this goal: approving needs a role codex-maple-1a2b3c4d does not hold and codex-maple-1a2b3c4d may be its author (the goal's rules). The host gives roles." The first clause is false.
6. Person's message via Failure::for_person: "Maple can't approve this result in "Static site search": approving needs a reviewer other than the author and Maple is not one (the goal's rules). The host, Harbor's owner, gives roles." Literally true, but the closing line sends the person to the host for a role Maple already has; `role give` would then answer "the member already holds this role".
second.fix: Change code, and add the case to the plan (Phase 5 "Rules" bullet says a role is always "a role WHO does not hold" and mockup P5-2 has no author-excluded line). Smallest precise fix: in the ReviewRecorded arm of the verifier (crates/locust-core/src/goal/fold.rs:585-611) the source-author set is already computed; record one more bool on RuleRefusal (the refused member is among those authors), copy it into Why::Rules at crates/locust-core/src/node/access.rs:252-258, and in rule_sentence / render (crates/locust-proto/src/api/level.rs:397-470, 248-268) when it is set say "approving needs a reviewer other than the author and Maple is the author" (agent's voice: "a role, held by a member other than the author, and WHO is the author", as the Members arm at level.rs:425-433 already does) and end with "Nothing to change; pick other work." instead of "The host gives roles." Keep the P5-2 lines when it is not set. If no new field is wanted, a wording-only change in the same two functions must stop asserting "a role WHO does not hold" whenever except_author is true and must not end with only "The host gives roles." Add a level.rs test that pins both voices for Role + except_author where the member holds the role and is the author; rules_and_state_never_suggest_a_level only checks absent words.
second.person_sees: An agent that is already a reviewer tries to approve its own work and is told it needs a role it does not have and that the host gives roles. It may ask you, and you may ask the host, for a role it already holds; nothing the host can give would let it approve its own result.
second.reason: Read the path end to end and found no step that fails. review_record (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/tasks.rs:226-251) signs a ReviewRecorded candidate with no own-result guard; sign_for (node/authoring.rs:98-134) replays it; fold.rs:590-611 refuses through may_review_with_authors (rules.rs:291-309: `(!exclude_author || !authors.contains(&principal)) && matches(by, ...)`) and records only what completion_qualifies returns, (Role{reviewer}, true) for the panel rule (rules.rs:245-255). access.rs:249-258 forwards exactly those three values, so render cannot know whether the role or the authorship failed. level.rs:416-424 writes "a role {who} does not hold" for every Role selector in the agent's voice and only hedges the author clause; level.rs:258-267 ends with "The host gives roles." whenever the selector names a role. The default-reviewer claim holds: selected_role returns counting_role unless --no-role (crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:63-75) and initial_reviewers prints "members you add or invite become reviewers" (roles.rs:99-110), so under review-panel a holder-who-is-author is the normal case of this refusal, not a corner. No test pins the opposite: rules_and_state_never_suggest_a_level (level.rs:786-847) runs Role + except_author but asserts only that "level", "allow", "locust" are absent; the byte-for-byte tests use reviewer_rule() with except_author false (level.rs:685-696); presentation.rs:2041-2050 only checks that printed commands parse. Nothing marks it intended: plan Phase 5 (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:3287-3306) specifies the role wording without an author case, mockup P5-2 line 3 is a non-holder, the companion (plan-details 331-384) has no per-rule sentences, and build-notes departure 2 says the rule sentences were inferred from P5-2. Severity stays medium: the refusal itself is right and nothing wrong is signed, but the phase's deliverable is a true one-sentence reason with who can change it, and here the agent's reason is false and the remedy in both voices points two people at a role change that cannot work.

first.title: A mistyped role on goal invite still shows no list of the goal's roles
first.scenario: The host of a goal with roles lead and reviewer runs `locust --owner goal invite --goal G --role reviewers`. The daemon answers invalid "this goal has no such role" with details {"role":"reviewers"} and no list. The terminal shows "locust: invalid: this goal has no such role Role: reviewers". The same typo on `role give` shows "... Role: reviewers Roles here: lead, reviewer". The review finding (goals.rs:170) names both commands: "After mistyping a role in role give or goal invite they are told the goal has no such role, with no list of the roles it does have."
first.evidence: role_details prints "Roles here:" only when the details carry a roles array (cli/mod.rs:172-195). goals.rs:354 sends {role, roles}; invitations.rs:180-183 sends {role} only. The R5 notes (lines 51-56) say the person "sees which role and which roles the goal has"; the test a_role_refusal_names_the_role_and_the_goals_roles_for_the_person covers role give only.
first.fix: Change the code: add "roles": entry.state().roles.keys() to the details at invitations.rs:182, and a test for goal invite beside the role give one.
first.person_sees: After mistyping a role in goal invite you are told the goal has no such role and shown the name you typed, but not the roles the goal does have. Role give shows the list.

second.statement: The unknown-role refusal in goal_invite (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/invitations.rs:179-184) carries details {"role"} only, so the terminal prints the mistyped name but no "Roles here:" list; role give's refusal (goals.rs:352-354) carries {"role","roles"} and prints both. The same daemon site also serves `goal add --role`, so both commands miss the list, and the R5 notes' claim that the person "sees which role and which roles the goal has" holds for role give only.
second.scenario: 1. Host has a goal with roles lead and reviewer. 2. `locust --owner goal invite --goal G --role reviewers`: goal_invite in crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1232 builds invite_plan; roles::selected_role (crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:71-73) returns the typed name unchecked, so the plan reads "Invite someone to "G" (...) as a reviewers ..." and asks "Proceed? [y/N]" (confirm.rs:99-112). 3. The person answers y; Request::GoalInvite{role: Some("reviewers")} reaches the daemon; goal_invite passes host(), the halt check and deciding(), then at invitations.rs:179-183 returns Invalid "this goal has no such role" with details {"role":"reviewers"}. 4. Failure::from keeps details_json (failure.rs:116-121); for_person leaves a non-Refused details object alone (failure.rs:199-204); print_failure + role_details (cli/mod.rs:159-195) print "locust: invalid: this goal has no such role Role: reviewers" with no "Roles here:" because there is no roles array. 5. Same result for `locust --owner --agent A goal add --goal G --role reviewers` (add_plan only_you.rs:808 -> GoalInvite at only_you.rs:273-281). 6. `role give ... reviewers` on the same goal prints "... Role: reviewers Roles here: lead, reviewer".
second.fix: Code should change, one line: in Node::goal_invite (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/invitations.rs:182) send .with_details(json!({"role": role, "roles": entry.state().roles.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>()})), the same shape role_change sends at goals.rs:354; role_details already prints it through presentation::safe. Add a CLI test beside a_role_refusal_names_the_role_and_the_goals_roles_for_the_person (crates/locust/tests/cli.rs:2218) that answers Request::GoalInvite with those details, or assert the details in an_invitation_role_is_given_on_admission_and_an_authority_role_is_refused_at_issue (node/tests/roles.rs:438). Optional, not needed to close it: have roles::selected_role refuse a typed role absent from view.roles so the refusal comes before "Proceed?". No plan change needed: companion row 306 only says `invalid` for an invitation role with no list.
second.person_sees: If you mistype a role when inviting someone or adding your own agent, you are first asked to confirm the invitation with the wrong role name in it, and after you say yes you are told the goal has no such role and shown what you typed, but not which roles the goal does have. The same typo on role give does show the list. Nothing is lost or changed; you have to run goal status to find the right name.
second.reason: Read the code at HEAD a4a5b55 (only docs changed since 9c337df). invitations.rs:179-184 builds details json!({"role": role}); goals.rs:352-354 builds {"role","roles"}. role_details (crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:170-195) appends "Roles here:" only when a roles array is present. No earlier check stops the request: selected_role (cli/roles.rs:63-75) returns the typed --role without comparing it to view.roles, and both invite_plan (only_you.rs:1210) and add_plan (only_you.rs:808) use it; "reviewers" is a well-formed role name, so only the daemon's contains_key check refuses it. Details survive to the printer (connection.rs:34, failure.rs:116-121) and for_person does not rewrite them (failure.rs:199-204). No test pins the opposite: the node test (tests/roles.rs:438-452) checks only the code Invalid for an absent role, and the CLI test (tests/cli.rs:2218-2271) fakes RoleGive only. Not recorded as intended: the R4 review finding goals.rs:170 (research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:610, 616) names goal invite explicitly ("Same pattern at invitations.rs:180-191", "role give or goal invite ... with no list"), and the R5 notes (research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md:51-56, item 11 at 194-196) claim the list is shown without excepting invite. The review's own "smallest fix" only changed print_failure and wrongly assumed that covered the list at all four sites, which is why the builder's faithful implementation left this gap. The plan itself does not demand a list here (plan-details row 306 vs row 303 for role.give), so this is an incomplete review fix, not a plan departure; low severity stands. Two additions to the reported scenario: the person is asked "Proceed?" on a plan naming the bad role before the refusal, and `goal add --role` shares the gap.

first.title: A joining agent's status line shows only its local name; mockup P5-1 shows its name in the goal too, and the notes claim a byte-for-byte match
first.scenario: The person runs `locust --owner goal join --name Juniper TICKET` for the agent claude-juniper-77aa0c52 and then `locust --owner status` before admission arrives. Mockup P5-1 (plan line 539) prints "Juniper (claude-juniper-77aa0c52) · joining". The code prints "claude-juniper-77aa0c52 · joining". The daemon holds the name asked for: goal_join stores it in the join record.
first.evidence: goal_summaries takes the name from state().members and falls back to the local name (views.rs:145-150); JoinRecord.name (local.rs:50, written at requests/invitations.rs:389-392) is not read. agent_lines prints one name when the two are equal (presentation.rs:701-707). The presentation test was fitted to the code: the joining summary is given the name "claude-juniper-77aa0c52" (presentation.rs:1770-1778) and the expected text has "  claude-juniper-77aa0c52 · joining" (line 1808), while the build notes say status "prints mockup P5-1 byte for byte" (notes lines 87-92). Not among the declared departures.
first.fix: Change the code: fall back to entry.local.joins.get(member).name before the local name in views.rs:145-150, give the test's joining summary the name "Juniper" and the mockup's line, and correct the field comment at api.rs:1478. The plan stays.
first.person_sees: While an agent waits to be let into a goal, status shows it only by its long local name, not by the name you chose for it in that goal.

second.statement: While an agent is joining (or refused), `Node::goal_summaries` fills `GoalSummary.name` with the local name and never reads the name the person asked for, which the daemon holds in `JoinRecord.name`; status therefore prints "claude-juniper-77aa0c52 · joining" where mockup P5-1 (plan line 539) prints "Juniper (claude-juniper-77aa0c52) · joining". The presentation test was fitted to the code and the build notes' "byte for byte" claim is wrong for that line; it is not among the twelve declared departures.
second.scenario: 1. `locust --owner goal join --name Juniper TICKET` for local agent claude-juniper-77aa0c52, with a ticket whose host is another computer that has not yet admitted. goal_join writes JoinRecord { name: "Juniper", .. } (requests/invitations.rs:385-399) and answers Membership::Joining. 2. `locust --owner status`. Entry::membership returns Joining because local.joins holds the principal (views.rs:31-36); state().members has no record for it, so views.rs:145-150 falls back to abilities.name, the local name. 3. agent_lines sees summary.name == local name and prints one name (presentation.rs:702-707): "  claude-juniper-77aa0c52 · joining". The mockup's line is "  Juniper (claude-juniper-77aa0c52) · joining". When --name is omitted the asked name is the local name (only_you.rs:160-169), so the one-name line is then correct; the gap shows only when the person chose a name. The same fallback gives a refused agent its local name only.
second.fix: Change the code; the plan stays. In `Node::goal_summaries` (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:145-150) take the name from state().members, else from `entry.local.joins.get(member)` (`JoinRecord.name`), else the local name. In crates/locust/src/cli/presentation.rs give the joining fixture the name "Juniper" (line 1773) and expect "  Juniper (claude-juniper-77aa0c52) · joining" (line 1808). Reword the field comment at crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:1478 ("the name asked for until admitted") and regenerate docs/reference/generated/runtime.contract.json, which carries that sentence at line 14583. Correct the "byte for byte" sentence in research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md lines 87-92 or leave it true after the fix. A daemon test that joins with a chosen name and reads status would pin it. The only other reader of GoalSummary.name is waiting_for, which skips non-members, so nothing else changes; a refused agent also gains the asked name, which is harmless.
second.person_sees: While an agent waits to be let into a goal, status lists it only by its long local name. The name you chose for it in that goal does not appear until the host's computer admits it.
second.reason: I could not refute it. Read: views.rs:103-160 (goal_summaries takes name from state().members, else abilities.name; joins never consulted); views.rs:30-37 (a held JoinRecord makes the agent Joining or Refused, so it is by definition not in state().members); local.rs:45-58 (JoinRecord.name exists); requests/invitations.rs:311-336 and 385-399 (goal_join stores the chosen name, and updates it on a retry); only_you.rs:72-74 and 154-177 (goal join has --name; default is the local name); peers.rs:355-360 (admission signs request.name unchanged, so the asked name is what the name in the goal becomes); presentation.rs:701-707 (one name printed when equal) and 1770-1778, 1808 (fixture name is the local name and the expected line lacks "Juniper"); authorization.rs:465-476 (status really lists a Joining summary after goal.join, so the state is reachable). The plan agrees with the mockup, not the code: line 521 says an agent is shown by its name in the goal with its local name beside it and that Juniper is joining; lines 3384-3393 give "NAME (LOCAL NAME)" per agent with the standing replacing roles and level for a joining agent; line 3336 defines GoalSummary.name as the name in the goal with no joining exception; the companion (details line 368) says the test compares with mockup P5-1. The only sign of intent is the builder's own field comment at api.rs:1478 ("its local name until admitted"), which is not in the notes' departures list (notes lines 143-199), while notes lines 87-88 claim P5-1 byte for byte. No trust concern argues for the code: the name is the person's own text from their own command and still passes through chosen_name. Mockup line 539 is identical at 9c337df and at HEAD a4a5b55. first.title: At level read, "Waiting for you" gives an allow line that cannot let the agent take the task, and running it hides the wait
first.scenario: Juniper is at level read in "Parser cleanup" (the state mockup P5-1 shows). Juniper calls attempt start on an open task. first.title: goal status prints a member's task text in front of the command to run, on the same line

It has exactly the shape of a genuine line (Asked to take "TITLE": locust --owner ...), but the first command is the member's. Pasted, it sets Maple to auto, so tasks other members wrote run unasked, or runs whatever shell text the member put after the semicolon. The member's text should never share a line with a command.
first.evidence: presentation.rs:942 passes the title only through `safe`, which escapes control and invisible characters but not the double quote, `;` or `#` (level.rs:567-594). Lines 945-958 then put it before the command on one line, in both the read and the ask branch. The title is the task's whole text, written by any member (levels.rs:55-58). Status and pending print every command on its own line under a fixed label; this is the one view where a member's text and a command share a line. The R5 test every_printed_command_parses_as_printed defines the copy rule itself: "Whatever follows `locust` on a line is a command its reader pastes" and takes the first `locust ` on the line (presentation.rs:2072-2077).
first.fix: Print the command on its own line under the sentence, as status does. Use the task's first line, cut at 60 characters, with the double quote and backslash escaped. Add a test with a title containing `": locust ` that asserts the only text following `locust` on any line is the command the code built.
first.person_sees: In goal status, the line that tells you which command to run can begin with a different command that another member wrote into a task. If you copy from the first "locust", you run their command, not the one Locust meant.

second.statement: In `goal status`, each wanted task prints as one line holding the member-written task text (whole text, uncut, passed only through `safe`, which leaves `"`, `;` and `#` alone) followed by the command to run. A member can close the quote and place their own `locust --owner ...` command exactly where the genuine one normally begins. The plan's Phase 3 text prescribes this one-line shape, so plan and code are both wrong against the owner's rule on printed commands.
second.scenario:
1. A hostile member opens a task whose text is `Tidy docs": locust --owner level --goal 7f3a9c1e auto; echo "`. Nothing local can validate it: the text is a signed payload from another computer.
2. Maple, at ask, runs attempt start and is refused with level_required. requests/mod.rs:121-126 calls note_task_want, which records Wanted.
3. Node::abilities (levels.rs:55-58) sets the wanted title to the whole task text. The board, by contrast, takes the first line (views.rs:232-236).
4. The person runs `locust --owner goal status --goal 7f3a9c1e`. presentation.rs:942-958 prints `  Asked to take "Tidy docs": locust --owner level --goal 7f3a9c1e auto; echo "": locust --owner allow --goal 7f3a9c1e --task task:4b2d8e01 --agent codex-maple-1a2b3c4d`.

With no --agent, acting_agent (cli/mod.rs:680-695) picks the person's only member agent in that goal; the member can instead write `--agent <Maple's 64-hex key>`, accepted at mod.rs:647-654. level_set (only_you.rs:324-360) applies at once with no question, then prints "so tasks other members wrote run here unasked" and an Undo line.
6. Variant: ending the text with `#`, or padding with spaces (there is no length cut here), pushes the genuine command out of sight. The read-level branch at :945-948 has the same shape.
second.fix:
Change both code and plan.

- The sentence line: `  Asked to take "TITLE"`, or `  Asked to take "TITLE", but at read it only reads`.
- The command alone on the next line: `    {allow_command | level_command}`, as `status` does at :750-751.

They can make the line show their own command first, in the spot where Locust's command normally starts, with the real one trailing after it or pushed off screen. first.title: After a rules change, document revisions awaiting review vanish from every reviewer's pending list though the engine still counts their reviews
first.scenario: Peer-review goal. Maple posts a plan revision D (DocumentRevised, context {Document(plan), round R1}); it is in Juniper's pending.to_review. The host runs `rules bind`, so current_rules becomes R2. wants_review(D) now returns false because current_context(Scope::Document) is {.., R2} (goal/mod.rs:299-306), so D leaves to_review, the pending counts and wait for every reviewer, including members admitted later. Yet D is still live in the engine: a review of D is accepted and counts, D can be picked, and the pick becomes the document's text.
first.evidence: wants_review applies `entry.goal.current_context(context.scope) != Some(context)` to all scopes (views.rs:598-601). The engine applies the current-round test only to tasks: flow.rs:484-491 (`if let Scope::Task(task) = context.scope && current_round != context.round`). The ReviewRecorded check (fold.rs:585-...) never calls active_context; approval resolves the subject's own rules (fold.rs:1026-1051); review_record and scope_select use the subject's own context (requests/tasks.rs:236, 292); document selection falls back to earlier rounds (projection.rs:463-479). Before 9c337df the filter had no round test (git show 9c337df^:crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs lines 419-436). The R4 review's fix for views.rs:419 said "for a task-scope context keep the item only when current_context == Some(context) ...; for goal and document scopes mirror the close test" (research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:223). The code comment "the engine signs no request there" is untrue for documents. The new test lifecycle.rs:237-327 covers tasks only.
first.fix: Code should change: move the current_context test into the Scope::Task arm of wants_review (workspace proposals are already limited to the current epoch at views.rs:495-503). Add a node test: revision posted, rules bind, the revision is still in the reviewer's to_review.
first.person_sees: After the host changes a goal's rules, plan or document changes that were waiting for approval silently drop off every agent's to-do list. Nobody is asked again, so the change stays unapproved unless someone notices.

second.statement: Since 9c337df, `wants_review` (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:598-601) drops every unapproved goal-scope finding and document revision from all reviewers' `pending.to_review` and counts as soon as any new rules binding lands, although the engine still asks for, accepts and counts reviews of them and still lets them be picked. The trigger is wider than the report says: it also covers goal-scope findings, and the first `workspace init` signs a rules binding too.
second.scenario:
1. Peer-review goal, rules R1. Maple runs doc revise on the plan: `doc_revise` stamps context {Document(plan), R1} (requests/documents.rs:40-43). Juniper's pending lists it under "Review needed" (can_review resolves the revision's own round, goal/mod.rs:437-480).
2. The host runs `rules bind` (or the first `workspace init`, which calls Request::RulesBind when the formation has no workspace part, cli/workspace.rs:536-594). chain.rs:225 sets snapshot.rules to the new record and chain.rs:270 sets current_rules = R2.
3. Juniper's next pending: `current_context(Scope::Document(plan))` is {.., R2} (goal/mod.rs:299-306), so `wants_review` returns false at views.rs:599 and the revision is filtered out at views.rs:513. It leaves to_review, PendingCounts.to_review and the brief for every reviewer. The same happens to a goal-scope finding posted under R1, since Scope::Goal shares the arm.
4. The engine still treats the revision as live: `desired_effects` applies its round test to tasks only (flow.rs:484-491), so a member admitted after the bind still gets a host/author-signed RequestReview for it (review_templates, flow.rs:229-290) and sees a "Delivery: review request" line but no "Review needed" entry. `review record` on it signs and is effective (ReviewRecorded arm, fold.rs:585-611, calls `subject` and the reviewer test, never `active_context`); `approval` resolves the revision's own round (fold.rs:1026-1051); a Select in {Document, R1} is valid because `decision` calls `active_context` only for Workspace (fold.rs:911-913); with no R2 selection it becomes the document text (projection.rs:463-479).
5. No other list tells anyone: there is no `behind` list yet (that is Phase 8). Only `doc read` proposals and the old delivery line still mention the revision.
second.fix: Code should change, not the plan. In `wants_review` (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:598) move the `entry.goal.current_context(context.scope) != Some(context)` test into the `Scope::Task(_)` arm, leaving the Goal/Document/Workspace arm with the closure test only (workspace proposals are already limited to the current epoch at views.rs:495-503). Correct the two comments (views.rs:511-512 and 596-597) so they claim the round test for tasks only. Add a node test beside `results_on_a_closed_picked_or_revised_task_are_in_nobodys_review_list` (node/tests/lifecycle.rs:237): post a document revision and a goal-scope finding, run RulesBind, assert both are still in the reviewer's to_review, including a reviewer joined after the bind. Phase 8 can reintroduce the drop for agreed documents together with its `behind` notice.
second.person_sees: After the host changes a goal's rules, or turns on shared files for the first time, plan changes and findings that were waiting for approval drop off every agent's "Review needed" list and review count. No agent is asked again and the author is not told, so the change sits unapproved until someone happens to look at the document's proposals and reviews it by its id. Nothing is deleted and a review typed by hand still works.
second.reason: I could not refute it; every step holds in the code at HEAD. views.rs:598-601 applies the current-context test to all scopes before the match; goal/mod.rs:299-306 maps Goal and Document scopes to state.current_rules, which chain.rs:225 and 270 replace on every effective RulesBound. `git show 9c337df^:crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs` (filter at lines 419-436) had no round test, so this is a regression from the R5 commit. The engine side is as claimed: flow.rs:484-491 restricts the round test to `Scope::Task`; fold.rs:585-611 (ReviewRecorded) and fold.rs:897-920 (decision, active_context only at 912-913 for Workspace) do not fence old rules rounds; requests/tasks.rs:236 and 292 use the subject's own context; projection.rs:463-479 falls back to earlier rounds' selections. So the comment at views.rs:511-512, "the engine signs no request there", is false for goal and document scopes. Nothing declares this intended: the R4 review's fix text (research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:223) asked for the current-context test on task scope only and "mirror the close test" for goal and document scopes; the builder's notes (research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md:73-74) describe only "while its task's round is open"; the plan defines a finding or document revision posted before a rules change as work under earlier rules and says "a change of rules strands no work" (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2306-2316). The only place the plan puts waiting revisions behind after a binding is Phase 8 (lines 4336-4343), which is not built, applies to agreed documents, and pairs it with a `behind` notice in pending. No test pins the opposite: lifecycle.rs:237-327 covers tasks only, and context.rs:630-700 binds rules before posting its finding. Two additions to the report: Scope::Goal findings are dropped the same way, and cli/workspace.rs:536-594 makes the first `workspace init` a trigger. Medium stands: silent loss of a to-do item with no data loss, since `doc read` proposals (requests/documents.rs:22-27), the delivery line (views.rs:572-590) and review by id still work.

first.title: The waiting line and task_title carry the whole task text, not the task's title
first.scenario: A member opens a task whose text is "Fix the parser\n\nRewrite the tokenizer ... (40 lines)". Maple, at ask, tries to take it. `locust --owner status` prints, as its first entry, `Maple wants to take "Fix the parser\u{a}\u{a}Rewrite the tokenizer ... (the entire brief on one line)" in "Static site search"`. Mockup P5-1 shows only "Fix the parser". The same whole text is sent twice in every status answer (abilities.wanted_tasks[].title and waiting[].kind.task_title), to the person and to the agent's tool, and status is read by most commands. A member who writes a very long task fills the top of the person's status.
first.evidence: waiting_for copies `task_title: wanted.title.clone()` (views.rs:197). WantedTask.title is built from the whole payload: requests/levels.rs:55-58 `entry.text(&self.store, event, None)`, where the board takes the first line (views.rs:232-236 `text.lines().next()`). Refused.task_title has the same source (access.rs:170-173). waiting_sentence quotes it with `safe` and no cut (presentation.rs:646-664; `quoted` at 415-417). The new test asserts only `starts_with("Read and implement")` (tests/daemon.rs:258-263) on a fixture whose text is "Read and implement\nAcceptance details" (tests/lifecycle.rs:92), so it passes with either the title or the whole text; t2_flow and the presentation fixture use one-line tasks.

first.title: "Waiting for you" lists wants that no longer wait: a disconnected agent's (the printed line is refused) and a task the agent has since taken
first.scenario: (a) Maple at ask asked for T; the person disconnects Maple (`agent revoke`). Status still opens with "Maple wants to take T" and the allow line; run as printed it fails with "... is disconnected. Connect it again ...". `pending` for the same goal lists nothing for Maple. (b) Maple at ask asked for T; the person sets Maple to auto (the refusal itself offers this); Maple takes T; later the person sets ask again. Status says "Maple wants to take T" while Maple's attempt on T is running. (c) The host takes away the role that let Maple start T: the line stays, the allow succeeds, the start answers not_eligible.
first.evidence: waiting_for tests only membership, halt and level (views.rs:170-176). agent_revoke clears nothing and the agent stays a Member (requests/daemon.rs:110-128); the CLI refuses a disconnected agent (cli/mod.rs:666-667) and so does the daemon (access.rs:345-351 `principals.active`). A want is deleted only by disallow, leave or removal (requests/levels.rs:244, requests/goals.rs:526-530, commit.rs:425-428), never by a start that lands, and abilities() filters wants only on closed/completed/selected (requests/levels.rs:47-49). The same question in pending applies both missing tests: views.rs:339-342 (`self.principals.active(&principal).is_none()` skips) and views.rs:374-379 (`can_start`). The new test covers allow, disallow, close and level auto only.
first.fix: Code should change: build the waiting list with the tests ask_first uses (active agent, can_start), and drop a want once the agent holds a running attempt on that round or delete the Wanted record when its start lands. Add these cases to the daemon test.
first.person_sees: Status shows a line under "Waiting for you" that fails when run because the agent is disconnected, or that asks permission for a task the agent is already working on.

second.statement: `waiting_for` lists every stored `Wanted` record of a local Member below auto on a non-halted goal, without asking whether the agent is still connected, already holds a running attempt on the task, or may still start it under the rules. So "Waiting for you" can print an allow line that fails (disconnected agent) or that settles nothing (task already taken, or role taken away), which breaks the plan's own rule that the list "holds only what a command of the person settles" and the details doc's claim that an entry stays "only while it can still be taken".
second.scenario:
All three build from the code as described.
(a) Maple at ask calls start on T -> `level_required`, `note_task_want` writes `Wanted`. Person runs `locust --owner agent revoke --agent maple`. `agent_revoke` only sets `revoked` on the principal record; membership stays Member and the allowance stays. `status` still opens with "Maple wants to take T" plus `locust --owner allow --goal G --task T --agent maple`. Run as printed, the CLI refuses in `acting_agent` with "maple is disconnected. Connect it again: ..." (and a key-addressed call is refused by the daemon in `local_agent`). The same status output also prints the disconnected line with the reconnect command at the bottom, so the person is told twice, once misleadingly. `pending` for the goal skips Maple.
(b) Maple at ask asks for T (want stored). The refusal text offers "Set Maple to auto, or allow this task"; the person sets auto. Maple starts T; nothing in `attempt_start` or commit removes the `Wanted` record. Person sets ask again. The round is not closed, completed or selected, so `abilities()` still returns the want and status says "Maple wants to take T" while Maple's attempt on T is running and its session can keep reporting and posting at ask. `pending` shows nothing for T (same session: `already_running`; offered start: `can_start` false because the offer has an attempt).
(c) Under rules whose independent start needs a role, Maple at ask asks for T while holding the role (the level check runs after the rules check, so the want is only written when the rules allowed the start). Host runs `role take`. The line stays; `task_allow` checks only membership and task state, so the allow succeeds; Maple's next start answers `not_eligible`.
second.fix: Code should change, and the plan's `waiting_for` sentence (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:3362-3369) should gain the same conditions, since the builder followed that sentence to the letter. Smallest change, all in `Node::waiting_for` (crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:167): (1) skip the summary when `self.principals.active(&summary.member).is_none()`; (2) skip a want whose task appears in `summary.abilities.claims` (the agent already holds a running attempt on it); (3) skip a want unless `entry.goal.can_start(round.context, member, offer, &entry.definitions)` passes for `None` or for an offer addressed to the agent on the current round, the same test `pending_work_with_news` applies at views.rs:374-379. Cleaner alternative for (2): in `attempt_start` (requests/claims.rs:85) add `local::allowance_delete` to the tx when the stored record is `Allowance::Wanted`, so a later refused start writes a fresh want. Add the three cases to `status_lists_what_waits_for_the_owner_with_a_ready_command` (node/tests/daemon.rs:213).
second.person_sees: Status sometimes says an agent "wants to take" a task when that is no longer true. If you disconnected the agent, the command printed under the line fails and tells you to reconnect it. If the agent is already working on the task, or the host took away the role it needed, the command runs but changes nothing useful. Nothing is lost; the line is just out of date until the task is closed or you run the revoke form of allow.
second.reason: Read the code at a4a5b55 (one docs commit after 9c337df; code unchanged). `waiting_for` filters only on `membership != Member`, `halted`, `level >= Auto` (views.rs:170-176) and then emits one entry per `summary.abilities.wanted_tasks` (views.rs:187-207). `abilities()` drops a want only when the round is closed, completed or selected (requests/levels.rs:47-49) and reads the name through `principals.get`, revoked or not (levels.rs:21-25). `goal_summaries` does not filter revoked principals (views.rs:126-158) and `Entry::membership` does not look at revocation (views.rs:30-43); `agent_revoke` writes only the principal record (requests/daemon.rs:110-128), and the plan itself says a disconnected agent is still a member (plan line 3205). The printed command uses the local name (api/level.rs:534-540); the CLI's `task_allow` resolves it through `acting_agent` (cli/only_you.rs:384), which returns `disconnected_agent` for a revoked agent (cli/mod.rs:664-667, 739-745); the daemon refuses too via `local_agent` -> `principals.active` (access.rs:346-352). So (a) holds. For (b): the only allowance deletes are `task_disallow` (levels.rs:244), leave (goals.rs:526-530) and removal (commit.rs:425-428); `attempt_start` (claims.rs:85-146) writes a claim and no allowance change, and a retry on the same session returns `Claimed` before any level check (claims.rs:99-109), so the stale want is never refreshed or cleared. The existing test even pins that a want comes back after auto -> ask (tests/daemon.rs:314-319), but only for a task not started; no test covers a start in between, a revoke or a role change. For (c): `allowed` checks rules before level (access.rs:243-262 then 300-343), `task_allow` never calls `can_start` (levels.rs:181-232), `Why::Rules` maps to `NotEligible` (access.rs:176), and `role.take` exists (api.rs:454, 871). `pending` applies both missing tests (views.rs:339-342, 374-379), so the two views disagree. Intent: the plan says the list "holds only what a command of the person settles, and every entry carries that command" (plan 3332-3333, 3558) and the details doc says an entry stays "only while it can still be taken" (details line 41); neither the build notes nor the R4 fix record declares these cases intended. The plan's function sentence (3362-3369) omits the conditions, so this is a plan omission the code inherited rather than a builder slip. Severity low stands: display only, the failing command explains itself, and status already prints the reconnect line at the bottom (presentation.rs:795-796). Adjacent, not part of this verdict: at level read the same list prints an allow line although goal status knows an allowance does not help at read (presentation.rs:943-948).

The plan names this test for the behaviour: "also covers `waiting` and the invitation counts" and "an agent gets its own entries".

first.person_sees: nothing visible

second.statement: The two daemon tests the plan cites for "an agent gets its own entries" only ever have one local agent in the goal, so neither can tell whether the per-agent filter in `goal_summaries` exists, and no test asserts that an agent's `waiting` list or goal-entry count excludes another local agent. The claim that the filter can be removed with nothing failing is wrong: `fabricated_join_intent_never_grants_read_access_on_a_shared_daemon` would fail, but only through the byte order of two test keys.
second.scenario:
1. Remove the `.filter(|member| principal.is_none_or(|own| own == **member))` at crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:133-135.
2. `status_shows_the_owner_every_principal_and_an_agent_only_itself` and `status_lists_what_waits_for_the_owner_with_a_ready_command` still pass, as reported. The first reads an agent's status on a daemon with no goals (daemon.rs:162-170), then on a goal from `lifecycle::setup`, which enrolls one agent, "host" (lifecycle.rs:22). The second compares the single agent's waiting list with the owner's (daemon.rs:271).
3. `fabricated_join_intent_never_grants_read_access_on_a_shared_daemon` (tests/authorization.rs:406) fails at authorization.rs:469-476. The goal holds two local agents: the host, whose part record `goal_create` writes (requests/goals.rs:138), and the intruder, given a forged join and part record. `goal_summaries` walks a `BTreeSet<&PublicKey>` (views.rs:127), so entries come out in key-byte order. Under the fixed test entropy (`Counting::new(21)`) the host key is draw 2 (f708...) and the intruder key is draw 7 (fd9f...). `goals[0]` therefore becomes the host's entry with `Membership::Member`, where the test expects `Joining`.
4. Narrower regressions are caught by nothing. Example: `status` building `waiting` from `goal_summaries(None, ..)` while `goals` stays filtered. The same goes for any change in the number of random draws before those two enrollments that makes the intruder key sort first.
second.fix:
Test only; no code or plan change. Append to `status_shows_the_owner_every_principal_and_an_agent_only_itself` (crates/locust-core/src/node/tests/daemon.rs, after the revoke check at line 209):
- Make the host agent wanted on a task: `super::lifecycle::offered`, then an `AttemptStart` refused with `LevelRequired`, as daemon.rs:217-243 does.
- Add a second local agent with `super::authorization::join_local(&mut d, agent, goal, 2)`.
- Assert the second agent's status has `goals.len() == 1`, `goals[0].member == second` and an empty `waiting`.
- Assert the first agent's status has `goals.len() == 1`, `goals[0].member == principal` and `waiting.len() == 1`.
- Assert the owner's status has `goals.len() == 2`.
Put it in this test, not in `status_lists_what_waits_...`: that test indexes `summaries[0]` at daemon.rs:349-352, which a second member could displace. With this the check row at docs/roles-and-permissions-plan-details.md:372 becomes true as written.
second.person_sees: Nothing. The program shows each agent only its own goals and waiting lines today; the tests that are supposed to guard that would mostly not notice if it stopped.
second.reason:
What I checked, by reading only (no cargo or tests run):
- **Single filter.** The per-agent filter at views.rs:133-135 is the only one; `status` passes `actor.principal` straight in and builds `waiting` from the filtered summaries (requests/daemon.rs:27, :36).
- **Named tests.** Both use `lifecycle::setup` (lifecycle.rs:9-58), which has one local agent, so the filter is a no-op for them. This part of the finding is confirmed. daemon.rs is unchanged between 9c337df and HEAD a4a5b55.
- **Other agent-side status readers.** replica_tests.rs:797, sim/scenario.rs:45, sim/check.rs:95 and crates/locust/src/daemon/minimal.rs:312 each have one agent per goal or do not inspect `goals`/`waiting`. None would notice.
- **Where the finding is wrong.** It dismisses authorization.rs:465-475 because it indexes `goals[0]` without checking the length. That test does have two local agents in the goal and reads status as the second, so the outcome depends on which key sorts first.
- **Key order.** I traced the entropy draws: open (node/mod.rs:144), host enroll (requests/daemon.rs:88), goal create (goals.rs:54, :72, :75), invite (invitations.rs:200), intruder enroll. I then computed blake3 and ed25519 for draws 2 and 7 in memory. The host key sorts first, `PublicKey` orders by bytes (id.rs:75), and `Entry::membership` gives the host `Member` (views.rs:30-43), so the assertion at authorization.rs:469 would fail.
- **Confidence.** That ordering is my hand trace plus an in-memory calculation, not a test run. It is sensitive to the draw count: an intruder at draw 6, 8, 9, 10 or 11 would sort before the host and the test would pass.
- **Remaining gap.** The accidental guard does not cover `waiting`. Build-notes departure 1 (research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md:145) made `waiting_for` rely on already-filtered summaries, and no test pins that for an agent.
- **Intent.** Nothing in the plan, build notes or fix record says the thin coverage is intended; plan lines 3371 and 3478 and details line 372 claim this test covers it.

first.title: At level read, the "Waiting for you" line prints an allow command that does not let the agent take the task, and the plan's test never puts the agent at read
first.scenario: Juniper is a member at level read (the state mockup P5-1 shows). Its chat calls locust_attempt_start on an open task. The daemon answers level_required (level read, needs auto) and records the task as wanted. `locust --owner status` then lists `Juniper wants to take "T" in "G"` with `locust --owner allow --goal .. --task .. --agent ..` under it. The person runs that line: it prints `.. may take "T" in "G" until the host revises it.` and an Undo line, the entry disappears and status says `Nothing is waiting for you.` The agent's next start is refused again (level read, needs ask), and nothing is listed any more. It should either list no entry at read or print the level line, as goal status already does.
first.evidence: waiting_for skips only `summary.abilities.level >= Level::Auto` (views.rs:170-176) and always builds `allow_command` (views.rs:199-204). first.title: A member named after another member's full key makes --member pick the other member, and the removal plan hides it
first.scenario: Ana hosts goal G with Harbor (host's agent) and Maple, whose key is 0a1b2c3d...(64 hex). Eve already knows Maple's key (she has one agent in G, or shares another goal with Maple) and redeems a second ticket with `goal join --name <Maple's 64-hex key>`. Admission is automatic. Ana's goal status prints `Member: 0a1b2c3d...(64 hex) (9f8e7d6c) · remote`. Ana removes the odd member by the name she sees: `locust --owner member remove --goal G --member 0a1b2c3d...(64 hex)`. The value is resolved to Maple's key, the plan reads `Remove member 0a1b2c3d from "G"` (the first eight characters of what she typed), she confirms, and Maple is removed while Eve's agent stays. `role give` and `role take` resolve the same way and apply at once with no plan.
first.evidence: selectors.rs:88-90 `if let Ok(key) = value.parse() { return Ok(key); }` returns before any member is read, so the name tier (member_from_views, 132-176) never sees the value. A 64-hex name is a valid member name: event.rs:1011-1016 (non-empty, at most MAX_MEMBER_NAME_BYTES, trimmed, no control characters), limits.rs:67 (64), and it is the only check in JoinRequest::verify (invite.rs:451) and plan_join (peers.rs:351-362 signs request.name as given). Names print bare when plain ASCII (presentation.rs chosen_name, 232-251; status line at 847-850). The removal plan and result print only eight key characters and no name (only_you.rs:1303-1305 and the `Removed {}` line in member_remove). The fix combined the prefix tier with names (fix record row 2: "An exact key wins") but left the full-key tier in front; the plan's own purpose sentence at docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2735-2736 is "so nobody picks a member by naming an agent after its key". Not introduced by 2de65f0, but it is the same defect class the row says is fixed, at prefix length 64.
first.fix: Code and plan both. Simplest root fix: refuse a member name that is 8 to 64 hex digits (the existing `selectors::prefix` test) wherever a name is chosen: in the CLI before the plan (member_name, add_plan, goal create) with a plain sentence, and in plan_join on the host's computer (InvitationRefused), so no signed name can read as a key or a key prefix; no signed encoding changes. CLI-only alternative: in resolve_member do not return at line 88; treat the parsed key as one candidate beside signed-name matches and refuse when two different members match. Either way print the member's name in the `member remove` plan and result, and add a selector test with a member whose name is another member's full key.
first.person_sees: The host tries to remove (or take a role from) a strangely named member by typing the name shown in goal status, confirms a plan that shows the same first eight characters, and a different, innocent member is removed instead. The stranger stays in the goal.

second.statement: A member may sign in under a name that is another member's full 64-hex key; `--member` (and `--recipient`) then resolves that printed name to the other member, because `resolve_member` returns any parseable full key before it reads names, and the `member remove` plan and result show only the first eight key characters, which match what the person typed. The plan's letter ("a full key is taken as given", plan line 1426; companion row 312) allows this, but its stated guarantee at 2735-2736 ("nobody picks a member by naming an agent after its key") is not met at prefix length 64, so plan and code both need the change.
second.scenario: 1. Ana hosts G with Harbor and Maple (key K, 64 hex). 2. Eve knows K from an earlier membership (another agent of hers already in G, or any other goal shared with Maple; the ticket itself carries only the governance key, and a ticket is single-use, so she needs a fresh ticket plus prior knowledge). 3. Eve runs `goal join --name K`. `member_name` (only_you.rs:171), `Request::check` (api.rs:1046) and `JoinRequest::verify` (invite.rs:451) apply only `is_member_name` (event.rs:1011-1016: non-empty, at most 64 bytes, trimmed, no control characters), and `plan_join` (peers.rs:351-362) signs `MemberAdmitted { name: request.name }` with no person involved. 4. Ana's `goal status` prints `Member: K (9f8e7d6c) · remote · endpoint ...` because `chosen_name` prints plain ASCII alphanumerics bare (presentation.rs:235-244, 260-271, 847-850). 5. Ana pastes it: `locust --owner member remove --goal G --member K`. selectors.rs:88-90 parses K as a key and returns Maple's key without reading the member list. 6. `removal_plan` (only_you.rs:1303-1305) prints `Remove member 0a1b2c3d from "G"`, the first eight characters of what she typed and no name; she confirms. 7. first.title: rules bind from directed to review-panel makes every member a reviewer on tasks still open under directed, where a reviewer may approve its own result
first.scenario: Goal under the built-in `directed` formation: Harbor (host's agent, lead and reviewer), Juniper (given `reviewer` by hand), Cedar and Maple (no role). Some tasks are open. The daemon signs the binding and one RoleHolders record putting all four members on the existing `reviewer` list. The open tasks keep `directed`, whose completion rule is one approval by a `reviewer`, author not excluded. Role lists are goal-wide and read at the review's own anchor, so Cedar (or any member, honest or hostile) now posts a result on an open task and approves it itself, and it counts. Before the bind it needed Harbor or Juniper. Cedar's own result also appears in its own to-review list, so an unmodified agent does this too. It should either not widen a list that earlier rules still use with a different meaning, or say so before the person confirms.

Either (a) in `rules_plan` (only_you.rs:1454-1483), when the formation being replaced already gives the counting role duties and tasks are open under it, print what a ROLE does under those rules and that every member gets it there too (with `--no-role` and `task revise` as the ways out), or (b) in `Node::rules_bind`, give the role automatically only when the goal has no list for it yet or the replaced rules use it the same way, and otherwise print the `role give` lines as `--no-role` does. Add a test binding review-panel over a directed goal with an open task.
first.person_sees: After switching a running 'directed' goal to 'review-panel', every agent can approve its own result on the tasks that were already open, so those results count with no second pair of eyes. The confirmation only said that open tasks keep their old rules and that everyone becomes a reviewer.

second.statement: `rules bind` to rules with a counting role (review-panel's `reviewer`) puts every member on a goal-wide list that tasks still open under `directed` also read, and there one holder's approval is enough and the author is not excluded. So the review step the host set up on those tasks disappears, and neither the plan text nor the result says so. 4. Honest path: Cedar's unmodified agent finishes a task the lead offered it and posts its result. `can_review` now holds for Cedar on its own result (mod.rs:437-477, author not excluded), so the result is in Cedar's own to-review list (views.rs:509-530) and the agent approves it. Hostile path: an altered Cedar needs no offer, because replay only checks `publish: members` and the current round, with the attempt optional (fold.rs:492-524); it can also approve any result already on those tasks, or a finding posted under the old `directed` binding, since the review arm has no current-context check (fold.rs:584-610).
5. Replay resolves the task's own (directed) rules with the role list at the review's anchor (fold.rs:123-140, 1167), finds Cedar a holder (rules.rs:203-206), needs one match with the author allowed (fold.rs:1181-1194), and the result is approved. The task round becomes completed on every computer (projection.rs:209-232), which also stops further offers and attempts on it (mod.rs:432-436). Before the bind this needed Harbor or Juniper.

Add a test binding review-panel over a directed goal with an open task, asserting a no-role member's approval of its own result there does not count. The finding's option (a), a sentence in `rules_plan` with the automatic give kept, only informs the person and does not close it; the owner should choose between the two, since option (b) makes new review-panel work wait for `role give` in this one case.
second.person_sees: You switch a running 'directed' goal to 'review-panel' to get stricter review. The confirmation says open tasks keep their old rules and that everyone becomes a reviewer. What it does not say is that on the tasks already open, a reviewer may approve its own result and one approval is enough. So from then on each agent's result on those tasks is marked approved by the agent that wrote it, the task shows as completed, and the only check left is the lead's pick. Taking the role back later does not undo approvals already given.

The reviewer list is the host's agent alone. `goal status` prints `2 more reviewers are needed; members you add or invite become reviewers.` The step that works is `role give` to the two members already in the goal. The R4 review named this status sentence under finding `only_you.rs:1329`; the fix record row 8 says Fixed, but only the bind plan and result changed.
first.evidence: presentation.rs:895-923: when `missing > 0` on the host's computer the tail is always `members you add or invite become {role}s.`, with no check for members of `view.members` who do not hold the role. The review text (research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:366-372) asked for the `role give` advice in that case. The Give lines are printed once by `rules bind` (only_you.rs:1472-1479) and nowhere afterwards.
first.fix: In the status block, when the goal is hosted here and some member is not on the counting role's list, print the `role give` command for those members (as only_you.rs:1472-1479 does) in place of the add-or-invite tail. Extend `goal_status_names_the_host_members_and_roles_and_counts_missing_reviewers`.
first.person_sees: A host who chose to pick reviewers by hand is told by the status page to add or invite more people, when what makes results count is giving the reviewer role to members who are already in the goal.

second.statement: On the host's computer, `goal status` under a formation with a counting role always ends the missing-reviewers line with "members you add or invite become reviewers." and never looks at whether members already in the goal lack the role, so after `rules bind --no-role` or `goal add --no-role` it points the host at adding people when `role give` to existing members is the step that makes results count. One detail of the report is loose: the R4 fix did change the daemon (the default bind now gives the role to everyone), so this is what is left of review finding `only_you.rs:1329` on the opt-out paths, not a fix that did nothing.
second.scenario:
1. Host's agent Harbor creates a peer-review goal and adds Maple and Juniper (the exact setup of crates/locust/tests/t2_flow.rs:1201-1229).
2. Host runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation review-panel --no-role` and confirms. The node skips the role record (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:239 `if !no_role`); replay creates `reviewer` as [Harbor] (goal/chain.rs:539-541). The test pins this holder list at t2_flow.rs:1270-1283. The plan and result print `2 more reviewers are needed. The role's holders stay as they are.` plus two `Give the role:` lines (cli/only_you.rs:1467-1479), once.
3. Later the host runs `locust --owner goal status --goal G`. cli/mod.rs:531-535 loads the formation and calls `presentation::goal_status`; presentation.rs:895-923 computes missing = 2 + 1 - 1 = 2, `view.hosted_here` is true, and the line is `2 more reviewers are needed; members you add or invite become reviewers.` with Maple and Juniper listed above it as members with no role.
The same line prints after `goal add --no-role` / `goal invite --no-role`, after `role take`, and (read from code, no flag involved) when an invitation issued under peer-review, which carries no role (cli/roles.rs:62-74, node/peers.rs:360 `role: invite.role.clone()`), is redeemed after the default bind to review-panel: that invited member is not a reviewer, and the sentence says invited members become reviewers.
second.fix: Code, plus one plan clause. In `presentation::goal_status` (crates/locust/src/cli/presentation.rs:895-923), inside `missing > 0` and `view.hosted_here`, collect the members of `view.members` not in `view.roles[role]`. When there are any, print after the count one line per such member, `Give the role: locust --owner role give --goal {goal_id} --member {selectors::member_key_prefix(&view.members, key)} {roles::quote_role(&role)}`, the same form as only_you.rs:1472-1479. Do not simply replace the add-or-invite tail as the report proposes: keep it when those members are fewer than `missing` (both steps are then needed), and drop it only when they cover the shortfall. Leave the off-host tail (`the host adds or invites them.`) alone. Extend `goal_status_names_the_host_members_and_roles_and_counts_missing_reviewers` (presentation.rs:1443; its fixture has one member, so the current assertions stay true) with a second member who lacks the role, and keep `every_printed_command_parses_as_printed` passing. Add the clause to the plan's Phase 4 status sentence (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2743-2746) and note it under row 8 of research/v2-phase-r4-fixes-2026-10-06.md.
second.person_sees: A host who chose to pick reviewers by hand opens the goal's status page and reads that two more reviewers are needed and that people they add or invite become reviewers. The two members who could be made reviewers are already listed just above, and the command that would do it is not shown. It was shown once, when the rules were changed.
