first.title: The size refusal on rules bind gives advice that cannot work and does not mention --no-role
first.scenario: A goal has more members than one role record holds (about 507) and at least one member is not on the counting role's list, for example a peer-review goal bound to review-panel, or a review-panel goal with one member added with `--no-role`. Any `rules bind` without `--no-role` shows the plan `Everyone in the goal becomes a reviewer.`, the person confirms, and the daemon answers `limit_exceeded: The "reviewer" role has too many holders to fit in one role change. Use another role for this group.` Another role would receive the same full list and fail the same way; the only thing that works is `--no-role`. For `role take` the same sentence drops the plan's other cure (remove a member from the goal).
first.evidence: goals.rs:617-630 `role_list_error` has one sentence for give, take and bind. goals.rs:262-276 maps the bind's role record through it. The fix record row 6 itself says `--no-role` permits the binding. Plan line 3215-3217 words the refusal as `remove a member from the goal or use another role`.
first.fix: Give the bind its own sentence, for example `These rules would make every member a ROLE, and that is more members than one role change can carry. Bind with --no-role and give the role by hand.` For give and take keep the plan's wording including `remove a member from the goal`. Assert the bind wording in `oversized_role_give_and_take_report_a_plain_limit_and_sign_nothing`.
first.person_sees: Only in a goal of about 500 or more members: changing the rules is refused after the person confirmed, with advice (use another role) that would be refused the same way, and no mention of the flag that lets the change through.

second.statement: When `rules bind` cannot fit the automatic "everyone gets the counting role" record into one header, the daemon answers with the give/take sentence `The "reviewer" role has too many holders to fit in one role change. Use another role for this group.`; for a bind that advice cannot work (any counting role gets the same full member list) and the one thing that does work, `--no-role`, is not named. The same sentence on `role give`/`role take` also drops the plan's other cure, `remove a member from the goal`, which is the only cure that helps a take.
second.scenario: 1. A private goal has 508 or more active members (no member cap exists; the 16 KiB header holds about 507 keys for a role named `reviewer`). 2. At least one active member is not on the counting role's list: a peer-review goal about to be bound to review-panel (list is absent, so the daemon compares against `[host]`), or a review-panel goal with one member added with `--no-role`. If every member already holds the role the lists are equal (replay keeps them sorted, chain.rs:118-120) and the bind goes through, so this step is required. 3. The host runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation review-panel`. The CLI plan (only_you.rs:1480-1482) prints `Everyone in the goal becomes a reviewer.` with no size warning. 4. The host confirms. `rules_bind` (goals.rs:239-276) builds `holders` from every active member, sees it differs from the current list, signs `Body::RoleHolders` with the full list, `sign_at` fails with `EventError::TooLarge`, and `role_list_error` (goals.rs:617-630) turns it into `limit_exceeded: The "reviewer" role has too many holders to fit in one role change. Use another role for this group.` Nothing is signed. 5. Rules naming a different counting role fail identically, because `holders` is the full active-member list whatever the role is called and the old list for a new name is `[host]`. Only `--no-role` (or rules with no counting role) binds. 6. Separately, `role take` on a list of 509 or more prints the same sentence, where "use another role" means nothing and the working cure is `member remove`.
second.fix: Code change, in `role_list_error` in crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs: let the caller choose the sentence (a second argument or a second small function). The bind call at goals.rs:276 gets its own text, for example `These rules would make every member a "reviewer", and that is more members than one role change can carry. Bind again with --no-role to leave the role's holders as they are.` (prefer this ending over the reviewer's "give the role by hand", since giving by hand stops at the same cap; a daemon message naming a CLI command has precedent at node/identity.rs:163). The give/take call at goals.rs:408 gets the plan's full wording (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:3213-3218): `... Remove a member from the goal or use another role.` In `oversized_role_give_and_take_report_a_plain_limit_and_sign_nothing` (crates/locust-core/src/node/tests/roles.rs:326-329) assert the bind message contains `--no-role` and not `another role`; today it checks only the code. Optionally add one sentence to the plan's Risks bullet at line 3213 saying `rules bind` is refused the same way and `--no-role` lets it through. No plan decision is needed.
second.person_sees: Only in a goal with about 500 or more members: the person asks to change the rules, is told everyone will become a reviewer, says yes, and is then refused with advice to "use another role", which would be refused the same way. Nothing tells them that adding `--no-role` lets the change through. Nothing is changed or lost by the refusal, and agents' work is not affected.
second.reason: Read at HEAD a4a5b55. goals.rs:617-630: `role_list_error` has one sentence, used by both `rules_bind` (goals.rs:276) and `role_change` (goals.rs:408). goals.rs:239-253: the bind's `holders` is every active member and `previous_holders` falls back to `[host]`, so a different role name cannot shrink the list; the record is signed only when the two differ, and chain.rs:114-121 and 187-198 keep stored lists sorted, so "at least one member not on the list" is a real precondition and the finding states it. No earlier check stops it: the CLI plan (only_you.rs:1453-1483) has no size test and prints `Everyone in the goal becomes a ...`; the CLI's `map_err` after the call (only_you.rs:1570-1581) rewrites only `Conflict`; `Failure`'s Display (failure.rs:108-112) prints `limit_exceeded: <daemon message>` unchanged. No member cap exists in crates (no MAX_MEMBERS; limits.rs:11 is the only bound). The test roles.rs:260-346 builds exactly this state (521 holders plus one member admitted with `role: None`), pins `LimitExceeded` for the bind and that `no_role: true` then binds, but asserts message text only for give/take (`too many holders`, role name, no `header`), so nothing pins the bind wording either way. Intent: the fix record row 6 (research/v2-phase-r4-fixes-2026-10-06.md:30) says the refusal is intended and that `--no-role` permits the binding, which is the cure the message omits; the plan's bind paragraph (lines 2721-2728) is silent on size; the plan's Risks bullet (lines 3213-3218) words give/take as "remove a member from the goal or use another role", and the code kept only the second half. The wording arrived in ec1e078. The scenario, severity and fix direction stand as reported; I only tightened the example sentence.

first.title: With --no-role the plan says `0 more reviewers are needed` when the rule names the role inside an `any` selector
first.scenario: Custom formation whose completion is `reviews` by `{"kind":"any","selectors":[{"kind":"role","name":"reviewer"},{"kind":"role","name":"senior"}]}`, count 2, author excluded. Goal has the host's agent and two members. `rules bind --formation-json ... --no-role --plan` prints `0 more reviewers are needed. The role's holders stay as they are.` followed by two `Give the role:` lines. In fact nothing counts until two more members hold one of the roles. The same zero hides the missing-reviewers line in `goal status` afterwards.
first.evidence: organization/roles.rs:101-116 `review_roles` walks into `Selector::Any`, so `counting_role` returns `reviewer`. cli/roles.rs:77-90 `reviewer_requirement` matches only `by: Selector::Role { name }`, so `missing_reviewers` returns None and only_you.rs:1468 turns that into 0 with `unwrap_or(0)`. `any` is valid in a reviews rule (validation.rs:66-78).
first.fix: Make `reviewer_requirement` find the role inside `Selector::Any` the same way `review_roles` does (one shared walk in organization/roles.rs), or print no count when `missing_reviewers` is None. Add the case to the bind test.
first.person_sees: With a hand-written rule that lets either of two roles approve, the plan for `rules bind --no-role` says no more reviewers are needed, and then lists commands for giving the role; results do not count until the role is given.

second.statement: When a reviews rule names its role inside an `any` selector, `counting_role` finds the role but `missing_reviewers` returns None, and three callers turn that None into zero: the `rules bind --no-role` plan and result print `0 more reviewers are needed`, the `goal create` plan prints `0 more are needed`, and `goal status` drops its missing-reviewers line. The plan (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2727-2728) says the `--no-role` plan "says how many reviewers are missing", so the code should change, not the plan.
second.scenario:
1. A goal has the host's agent and two members, and its current rules have no `reviewer` list holding those members (for example a peer-review goal).
2. The host writes a formation that declares roles `reviewer` and `senior`, with completion `{"kind":"reviews","by":{"kind":"any","selectors":[{"kind":"role","name":"reviewer"},{"kind":"role","name":"senior"}]},"count":2,"exclude_author":true}`. Validation accepts it (crates/locust-core/src/organization/validation.rs:66-78; `fixed_members` returns None for roles, so no threshold error).
3. `locust --owner rules bind --goal G --formation-json '...' --no-role --plan` prints `0 more reviewers are needed. The role's holders stay as they are.` followed by two `Give the role: locust --owner role give ... reviewer` lines. Confirming prints the same text in the result.
4. After the bind, both role lists hold only the host's agent (crates/locust-core/src/goal/chain.rs:539-541), so the rule needs two more holders before every member's result can count. `goal status` shows no missing-reviewers line.
5. Same cause, not in the original finding: `goal create --formation-json` with this formation prints `Reviewers now: NAME (key, the host's agent). 0 more are needed; ...` (crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:103).
second.fix: In crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs, make `reviewer_requirement` match a `Reviews` part whose `by` names the role anywhere inside a `Selector::Any` (the walk `review_roles` already does in crates/locust-core/src/organization/roles.rs:101-116), and return the roles that selector names. Have `missing_reviewers` subtract the distinct holders across all of those roles, not only the counting role's list. The reviewer's first option alone (shared walk, same holder count) would swap the under-count for an over-count whenever the second role has other holders. The smaller stopgap is to drop the `unwrap_or(0)` in `rules_plan` (only_you.rs:1468) and `initial_reviewers` (roles.rs:103) and print no count when the result is None. Add the `any` case to the bind test in crates/locust/tests/t2_flow.rs (around line 1247) and to `goal_status_names_the_host_members_and_roles_and_counts_missing_reviewers`.
second.person_sees: With a hand-written rule that lets either of two roles approve, the plan for `rules bind --no-role` says no more reviewers are needed and then lists the commands for giving the role. Results do not count until two more members hold one of the roles, and the status page does not say any are missing. Starting a goal with the same rule also says no more are needed.
second.reason:
I read the code at HEAD a4a5b55; nothing was run. Every step of the scenario holds and nothing stops it earlier.

- **Role is found:** `review_roles` walks into `Selector::Any` (crates/locust-core/src/organization/roles.rs:101-116), so `counting_role` (roles.rs:129-135) returns `reviewer`.
- **Count is lost:** `reviewer_requirement` (crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:77-90) only matches `by: Selector::Role { name }`; an `Any` selector falls to `_ => None`, so `missing_reviewers` (roles.rs:91-98) returns None.
- **None becomes zero in three places:** crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1468 (bind plan, repeated in the result via `role_changes` at only_you.rs:1591-1597), crates/locust/src/cli/presentation.rs:898-904 (`goal status`, line hidden because `missing > 0` fails) and crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:103 (`goal create` plan).

- **No test pins the opposite:** the only assertions use the `review-panel` preset with a direct role (crates/locust/tests/t2_flow.rs:1247, presentation.rs:1476-1483).
- **Not intended:** the plan, the fix record (row 8 of research/v2-phase-r4-fixes-2026-10-06.md) and the R5 build notes say nothing about this case.
- **In scope:** the bind line came in with fix commit ec1e078; the `goal status` and `goal create` zeros predate it (8c086c1).

Low severity stands: it needs a hand-written formation, and the `Give the role` commands are still printed.

first.title: No test reads the role name the CLI adds to the kind-change refusal of rules bind
first.scenario: The R4 review finding `requests/goals.rs:168` had two halves: the wrongful refusal of an unused role (fixed and tested) and that the refusal did not say which role. The second half is fixed only in the CLI, which prefixes the role from the error's details. Remove lines 1569-1581 and every test still passes: the person would again see `conflict: this role is a group in this goal; these rules make it pick or close. Use another role name.` with no role named.
first.evidence: only_you.rs:1569-1581 is the only place the role name reaches a person. `rules_bind_is_refused_when_a_role_would_change_kind` and `rules_may_keep_an_unused_deciding_role_but_cannot_turn_an_unused_group_into_a_decider` (node/tests/roles.rs:214-257) assert only `ErrorCode::Conflict`; `git grep 'these rules make it'` finds the sentence only in goals.rs:172-174. Plan line 2567-2571 words the refusal with ROLE in it.
first.fix: In the node tests assert `details.role`, and in crates/locust/tests/cli.rs add a `rules bind` run whose stub answers the conflict with `{"role":"lead"}` and assert the printed line starts with `lead:`.
first.person_sees: Nothing today. If a later edit drops the role name from this refusal, no check would notice and the host would be told a role changes kind without being told which one.

second.statement: The prefix at only_you.rs:1569-1581 is untested, but it is not the only place the role name reaches a person: `print_failure` appends ` Role: NAME` from the same details for every command, and a CLI test pins that. What is really unpinned is the daemon attaching `{"role": ...}` to the kind-change refusal (goals.rs:176); and because both fixes landed, the refusal today names the role twice.
second.scenario:
1. Host runs `locust --owner rules bind` with rules that turn a listed group role into a picker or closer (or the reverse). `Node::rules_bind` answers conflict with details `{"role":"lead"}` (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:165-177).
2. The CLI's `rules_bind` prefixes the message with the role (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1569-1581, added in ec1e078), leaving details untouched.

5. Remove only_you.rs:1569-1581: all tests pass and the line still ends ` Role: lead`, so the reported outcome ("no role named") does not happen.
6. Remove `.with_details(json!({"role": role}))` at goals.rs:176 instead: all tests still pass (node/tests/roles.rs:215-257 assert only `ErrorCode::Conflict`; no node test reads `details_json` for any role refusal), and both the prefix and the tail vanish. That is the edit no check would notice.
second.fix: Two small changes, neither the CLI test the finding proposes (asserting the line starts with `lead:` would pin the duplicate). (a) In `rules_bind_is_refused_when_a_role_would_change_kind` (crates/locust-core/src/node/tests/roles.rs:215), keep the error from the first refused bind and assert its `details_json` parses to `{"role":"lead"}`; do the same for the named role in the second bind and in `rules_may_keep_an_unused_deciding_role_but_cannot_turn_an_unused_group_into_a_decider` (`judge`). (b) In the CLI's `rules_bind` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1569-1581), delete the `map_err` prefix: `role_details` in `print_failure` superseded it, already covers all four daemon sites, and is pinned by `a_role_refusal_names_the_role_and_the_goals_roles_for_the_person` (crates/locust/tests/cli.rs:2218-2269). This also stops the CLI rewriting `error.message` under `--json`.
second.person_sees: Today a host whose new rules would change what a role is gets told no, and the role is named twice on the same line: once at the front ("lead: this role is a group...") and once at the end ("Role: lead"). Nothing is lost and the name is correct. If someone later dropped the role name from the daemon's answer, no check would catch it and the host would be told a role changes kind without being told which.
second.reason:
Read only, at HEAD a4a5b55 (9c337df plus docs-only changes: `git diff --stat 9c337df a4a5b55` touches three docs files, no code). The cited block is as described: crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1569-1581 inside `rules_bind` (fn at :1507) prefixes `presentation::safe(role)` onto the conflict message. The node tests at crates/locust-core/src/node/tests/roles.rs:215-257 assert only `ErrorCode::Conflict`, and no test in crates/locust/tests/cli.rs stubs a rules-bind conflict (the rules-bind tests at :3073-3310 cover plans, files and invalid formations). So the test-gap half is true.

What decided "partly": the evidence claim that this block "is the only place the role name reaches a person" is false. crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:159-196 (`print_failure` + `role_details`, added by 9c337df) appends ` Role: NAME` and ` Roles here: ...` for any failure whose details carry `role`, regardless of command or error code, and every failure from `execute` goes through it (mod.rs:109-112). That path is pinned by `a_role_refusal_names_the_role_and_the_goals_roles_for_the_person` (crates/locust/tests/cli.rs:2218-2269, exact stderr with a bidi override escaped) and recorded as intended in research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md:51-56 and departure 11 (:194-196). `Failure::from(ApiError)` keeps `details_json` (failure.rs:115-121) and the `map_err` only edits `message`, so the tail fires for rules bind too. Removing :1569-1581 therefore leaves the role named; the scenario's stated outcome fails at that step.

Why both exist: the R4 review gave two overlapping fixes. research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:414-433 (goals.rs:168, fix session) asked for the CLI `rules_bind` prefix, landed in ec1e078; :606-614 (goals.rs:170, R5) asked for the generic tail in `print_failure`, landed in 9c337df. Neither commit removed the other, so the role prints twice. The fix record row 11 (research/v2-phase-r4-fixes-2026-10-06.md:35) mentions only the unused-role half.

The residual real gap is one link earlier: goals.rs:176 `.with_details(json!({"role": role}))` is read by no test (`git grep details_json` in node tests finds only levels.rs, for level refusals), and the CLI test feeds a hand-written stub, so dropping the details would pass every check and remove the name from both places. Whole text: levels.rs:55-58 and access.rs:170-173 call `entry.text(..)` (entry.rs:114-134, returns the full payload) while only `task_view` takes `.lines().next()` (views.rs:236); views.rs:197 copies `wanted.title` into `task_title`. Printing: presentation.rs:415-417 `quoted` is `"{safe}"` with no cut; presentation.rs:942-957 is `safe(title)` followed by the command on the same line; `safe` (level.rs:567-594) escapes controls, bidi and ignorables only, and its doc says nothing is shortened. No later pass rewrites the lines (render at presentation.rs:995-1003 returns them as built). `role give` is immediate and accepts a key prefix (roles.rs:1,13-23; only_you.rs:120 has no `confirm::flags`).
Not intended: the plan says a wanted task carries "its title" (plan 1921-1922) and that titles reach a person "only through `safe`, the titles quoted and cut" (plan 3551-3552; 3293-3295 says cut at 60 with "…"); mockups P5-1 (line 525) and P5-3 (line 592) show the short title; the companion's check table claims "Text written by other members cannot inject terminal controls or stretch a refusal" (details line 46). Only `render` in level.rs (308-314) cuts; the views do not. The builder's notes and the R4 review/fix records do not mention whole text or first line.
No test pins against it: the only wanted-task fixture in the CLI is "Fix the parser" (presentation.rs:1956-1960); the "Asked to take" line has no assertion anywhere; daemon.rs:258-263 uses `starts_with`; level.rs:868 pins the unescaped `in "Say "hi""`; the paste rule at presentation.rs:2072-2076 takes everything after the first `locust ` on a line, which is exactly what the hostile title hijacks.
Two corrections to the reported finding, neither weakening it: the same-line layout and the whole-text title come from Phase 3 (commit 3196be84; plan line 2028), and 9c337df rewrote those lines without closing it, so the plan line needs amending with the code; and the attack is stronger than written, because the payload can sit after a harmless first line (the board never shows it) and can be arbitrary shell, not just a `locust` command. Severity stays high: it directly breaks the owner's rule that no text from another computer can change what a printed command does, using only an ordinary member.

first.title: A member who names itself after another member's key prefix makes every printed --member command for that member fail, and the refusal recommends the same prefix
first.scenario: Ana hosts a goal with Juniper (key 8d03f2b6...). Mallory redeems a ticket with `goal join --name 8d03f2b6` (is_member_name accepts it; every member can see Juniper's key). Ana runs `locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member Juniper reviewer`; the output ends `Undo: locust --owner role take --goal c01d55aa --member 8d03f2b6 reviewer`. Run as printed it is refused: `invalid: member selector 8d03f2b6 is ambiguous; choose a key prefix: Juniper (8d03f2b6), 8d03f2b6 (9f3b2c1d)`. The prefix it tells her to choose for Juniper is the one that was just refused. The same happens to the `Give it back:` line, the host's-agent line, and the `Give the role:` and `Undo for one member:` lines of rules bind when Mallory copies that member's prefix. Before fix 2 (commit 2de65f0) the key-prefix tier answered first and these lines ran.
first.evidence: selectors.rs:118-131 `member_key_prefix` lengthens the prefix only until no other member's KEY starts with it; names are not considered. selectors.rs:138-151 `member_from_views` now puts signed-name, enrolled-name and key-prefix matches into one candidate set, and 155-171 builds the refusal from `member_key_prefix` again. The unit test pins the self-contradicting hint at selectors.rs:398-404 (`Juniper (01010101), 01010101 (02020202)` for the selector `01010101`). Printed lines that use the helper: roles.rs:126-133 `inverse`, only_you.rs:741 and 1474-1482. The corrected plan (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2734-2736) asks for the refusal but says nothing about the commands Locust itself prints. The fix record's row 2 says "Fixed".
first.fix: Code and plan both. Keep the refusal the plan asks for, and make `member_key_prefix` grow until the prefix is also not equal to any other member's signed name or local enrolled name (falling back to the full key), so a printed command and the refusal's suggestion never name a colliding prefix. Add the case to `a_member_resolves_by_key_prefix_then_name...` and to the role undo test, and one sentence to plan line 2734.
first.person_sees: The Undo line Locust just printed is refused as ambiguous, and the message tells you to use the very same letters you just typed. You can only get through by guessing to use the member's name or a longer key.

second.statement: A member whose signed name equals the lowercase key prefix Locust prints for another member makes every printed `--member PREFIX` command for that member (Undo, Give it back, the host's-agent line, Give the role, Undo for one member) be refused as ambiguous, and the refusal lists that same prefix as the one to choose. The plan says an Undo command "runs as printed" (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:1333-1336) and the fix that merged the name and key-prefix tiers (2de65f0) did not teach `member_key_prefix` about names. It fails closed: no wrong member is ever picked.
second.scenario:
1. Mallory already knows Juniper's key prefix 8d03f2b6 before joining (an agent's key is its member key in every goal, api.rs:410-415, so any earlier shared goal shows it; or Mallory holds a second ticket). This must be known at join time because a signed name cannot change afterwards; "every member can see the key" alone is not enough.
2. Mallory runs `goal join --name 8d03f2b6 TICKET`. only_you.rs:171, Request::check (api.rs:1045), JoinRequest::verify (invite.rs:451) and the host daemon's plan_join (peers.rs:308-362) check only is_member_name (event.rs:1011: non-empty, <=64 bytes, trimmed, no controls); nothing compares the name to names or keys. The host signs the admission unattended.
3. Ana runs `locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member Juniper reviewer`. roles.rs:126-133 `inverse` -> `unique_key` -> `member_key_prefix` prints `Undo: locust --owner role take --goal c01d55aa --member 8d03f2b6 reviewer` (no other KEY starts with 8d03f2b6, so the helper stops at 8 characters).
4. Ana runs that line. resolve_member (selectors.rs:88): 8 hex chars is not a full key. member_from_views (selectors.rs:137-152) collects Juniper (key prefix) and Mallory (name == value): two keys, so line 156 answers `invalid: member selector 8d03f2b6 is ambiguous; choose a key prefix: Juniper (8d03f2b6), 8d03f2b6 (9f3b2c1d)`.
5. The hint repeats the refused prefix. What still works: `--member Juniper` (if no second member copied that name too), a 9+ character prefix, or the full key; none of these is printed in human output (member_label always prints 8 characters), so the longer key comes only from `--json`.
Same for `Give it back:` and the host's-agent line (roles.rs:297-306), `Give the role:` (only_you.rs:739-741, 1474-1476) and `Undo for one member:` (only_you.rs:1481-1482). Before 2de65f0 the key-prefix tier returned first and all of these ran.
second.fix: Code and one plan sentence. In `member_key_prefix` (crates/locust/src/cli/selectors.rs:118-131) extend the per-length test so a length is also rejected when another member's signed name equals `full[..length]`, and replace `.expect("distinct full keys")` with a fall-back to the full 64 characters: a name may be 64 bytes (limits.rs:67), so a member can be named a whole key, and at 64 the exact-key parse at selectors.rs:88 wins before names are looked at; keeping the `expect` with the new condition would panic. That one change fixes all four printed sites and the refusal's own candidate list, since they all call this helper. Signed names are the only hostile input; enrolled local names are the person's own, so plumbing them in is optional. Update the pinned expectation at selectors.rs:398-404 (it becomes `Juniper (010101010), 01010101 (02020202)`), add the collision to `role_undo_lines_put_the_holders_back_and_name_the_member_by_key` (crates/locust/tests/cli.rs:2733), and amend plan lines 2699-2700 and 2734-2736 to say the printed prefix is one that no other member's key starts with and no other member is named.
second.person_sees: You give Juniper a role, copy the Undo line Locust just printed, and it is refused as ambiguous. The message tells you to choose a key prefix and shows, for Juniper, the exact letters you just typed. Nothing wrong happens to the goal, but you only get through by guessing to type the name instead, or by digging a longer key out of the JSON output.
second.reason: Read the code at HEAD a4a5b55 (crates unchanged since 9c337df). selectors.rs:118-131 lengthens the prefix only against other members' keys; selectors.rs:137-152 puts name and key-prefix matches in one set and 156-171 builds the hint with the same helper, so the collision and the self-repeating hint both follow directly. `git show 2de65f0 -- selectors.rs` confirms the old code returned from the key-prefix tier first, so this is new with fix 2. All four printed `--member` sites (roles.rs:128; only_you.rs:739, 1474, 1481) use `member_key_prefix`. No earlier check stops the state: is_member_name (event.rs:1011) accepts 8 hex characters and plan_join (peers.rs:308-362) compares no names. No test pins the opposite; the unit test at selectors.rs:398-404 pins the contradictory hint. The plan intends the refusal (2734-2736) but also requires that an Undo command "runs as printed" (1333-1336) and defines the prefix only against keys (2699-2700); neither the fix record (row 2, "Fixed") nor the R5 build notes mention the printed commands. Two corrections to the report: the attacker must know the prefix before joining because names are immutable (reachable, since agent keys are the same in every goal), and the proposed fix must drop the `expect`, not just add the name test. Severity stays medium: it breaks a stated plan guarantee and the rule that another computer's text cannot change what a printed command does, but it only refuses and never selects the wrong member.

first.title: A role name that begins with a dash is printed into role commands where the parser reads it as a flag, and role text is printed raw
first.scenario: The host runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal c01d55aa --formation-json rules.json --no-role` with a formation someone else wrote whose counting role is named `--help` (is_role_name, organization.rs:295, only asks for non-blank text without control characters). The plan and the result print, per member, `Give the role: locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member 8d03f2b6 --help`. Run as printed it shows the help page and gives nothing, so the goal stays short of reviewers. A role named `-reviewer` prints bare and fails with "unexpected argument '-r'"; `--x y` prints as `'--x y'` and still fails, because quoting does not stop clap from reading a leading dash.
first.evidence: roles.rs:112-121 `quote_role` treats `-` as a plain byte and never emits `--`; roles.rs:22 defines the positional as `Arg::new("role").required(true)` without allow_hyphen_values (args.rs:137 sets it only for the generated API positionals). Callers that print it: roles.rs:126-133, only_you.rs:738-742, 1474-1482. `quote_role` also does not pass the role through `safe`: at only_you.rs:738-742 the role comes from a ticket (`preview.role`, only_you.rs:1024-1030), so bidi overrides and zero-width characters, which is_role_name admits, reach the terminal unescaped inside a printed command. No test feeds a dash-leading role to `role_undo_lines_put_the_holders_back_and_name_the_member_by_key` or to `every_printed_command_parses_as_printed`.
first.fix: Code should change: print `-- ROLE` in every role command (the positional then takes any text), or refuse a leading `-` in is_role_name since nothing is deployed. For a role that is not plain ASCII, print no ready command and say why, rather than raw bytes. Add a dash-leading and a bidi role to the two tests.
first.person_sees: A printed "Give the role" or "Undo" line shows the help page or an error instead of changing the role, for goals whose rules name a role starting with a dash.

second.statement: `quote_role` prints a role name that begins with `-` as a bare or single-quoted word with no `--` before it, so every printed role command (`Give the role:`, `Undo:`, `Undo for one member:`, `Give it back:`) is read by clap as a flag and shows help or fails; it also prints the role's characters without `safe`, so bidi and zero-width characters reach the terminal inside a printed command. The second half is wider than reported: on `goal join` the role comes from a ticket whose signature is checked only against the key the ticket itself carries, so anyone who can hand a member a ticket chooses that text, not only the host.
second.scenario:
Dash, as reported: 1. A formation declares a group role named `--help` (or `-reviewer`, or `--x y`) and names it in a Reviews completion part. `is_role_name` (crates/locust-proto/src/organization.rs:295) only asks for non-blank text with no control characters, and it is the only check formation validation applies to role names (crates/locust-core/src/organization/validation.rs:24-33, 208-209), so `checked_formation` passes. 2. The host runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal c01d55aa --formation-json rules.json --no-role` in a goal with at least one member who does not hold the role. `rules_plan` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1454-1478) prints per such member `Give the role: locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member 8d03f2b6 --help`. Without `--no-role` the same role lands on line 1481-1482 as `Undo for one member: locust --owner role take ... --help`. 3. Run as printed, clap matches `--help` as the built-in help flag; crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:62-67 prints help and nothing is given. `-reviewer` prints bare (quote_role counts `-` as plain) and fails on unknown short `-r`; `--x y` prints as `'--x y'`, the shell hands clap one word starting with `--`, and it fails as an unknown long flag. A role named `--json` or `--owner` is taken as that global flag and the required positional is then missing. In no case does the command do something other than fail or show help or version, because the required positional `role` is never filled.

Raw text, corrected: 1. Anyone builds a ticket naming a goal the reader's agent is already in, puts their own key in `governance`, signs with it, and sets `role` to text holding U+202E or U+200B (admitted by `is_role_name`, checked at invite.rs:316-323). `Invitation::verify` (crates/locust-proto/src/invite.rs:274-285) checks the signature against `self.governance` only. 2. The reader runs `locust --owner goal join` with that ticket. `goal_join` (only_you.rs:1008-1031) decodes it, finds standing `member` from local status and returns `already_member_output(..., preview.role)` with no call that ties the ticket to the goal's host. 3. only_you.rs:732-743 prints `Give the role: locust --owner role give --goal G --member K '<raw role>'` through `quote_role`, which never calls `safe`. The join plan a few lines away (only_you.rs:980) does pass the same role through `safe`.
second.fix: Code and one plan sentence should change. In `quote_role` (crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:112): when the role starts with `-`, print `-- ` before the word (the role is the last argument in all four printed lines, and clap's `--` escape then fills the positional with any text); this keeps every pinned string and mockup unchanged for ordinary roles. Setting `allow_hyphen_values` on the positional at roles.rs:22 is not enough, since clap still matches known flags such as `--help` and `--json` first. Also in `quote_role`: when `presentation::safe(role) != role`, return no command (make it `Option<String>`), and have the callers at roles.rs:126-133, only_you.rs:738-742 and 1473-1482 print the role through `safe` with a sentence in place of the ready command. Amend plan lines 2701-2703 of docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md, which today list `-` as a plain character and say nothing of a leading dash or of escaped characters. Add a `--help` role and a U+202E role to `role_undo_lines_put_the_holders_back_and_name_the_member_by_key` (crates/locust/tests/cli.rs:2733), which already runs the printed lines through `sh -c`.
second.person_sees: In a goal whose rules name a role starting with a dash, the ready-made "Give the role" or "Undo" line shows the help page or an error when pasted, and the role is not changed. Separately, someone who pastes an invitation for a goal their agent is already in can be shown a "Give the role" line whose role text contains invisible or direction-flipping characters, so the line on screen may not read as what it is.
second.reason: Read, not run. `quote_role` (crates/locust/src/cli/roles.rs:112-121) treats `-` as plain, never emits `--`, never calls `safe`. The positional is `Arg::new("role").required(true)` (roles.rs:22); the only `allow_hyphen_values` uses are formation.rs:28, client.rs:34-36 and args.rs:137/242, none on this command, and no `mut_arg` touches it. The top-level parser is stock clap 4.6.7 with auto help/version and global long flags (args.rs:155-205), and mod.rs:62-67 turns DisplayHelp into printed help. Role names in a formation are checked only by `is_role_name` (validation.rs:24-33, 208-209; organization.rs:295), which admits `--help`, `-reviewer` and Cf characters such as U+202E. All three call sites print as cited (roles.rs:126-133, only_you.rs:738-742, 1473-1482), while neighbouring prose lines use `presentation::safe(role)`. No test pins the opposite: cli.rs:2733 uses only `review team's`, and `every_printed_command_parses_as_printed` (presentation.rs:1936-2110) renders no role command at all (its operation list is allow, attempt.start, context.read, delivery.acknowledge, event.show, invitation.revoke, level). Not intended: the plan (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2699-2703) specifies exactly this quoting, including `-` as plain, but the same plan requires these lines to run as printed (2903-2905) and the R5 build notes (research/v2-phase-r5-build-notes-2026-10-06.md:28-30, 55-56) say role names shown to the person go through `safe`; nothing in the R4 review or fix record accepts a dash-leading or unescaped role. What decided the raw-text half: invite.rs:274-285 verifies a ticket against the key inside the ticket, and only_you.rs:1008-1031 prints from it before any check against the goal's host, so the text is not limited to the out-of-scope hostile host. Severity stays low: `is_role_name` excludes control characters, the role stays one shell word, and the daemon refuses an unknown role (goals.rs:353), so the worst outcome is a command that fails or a misleading-looking line.

first.title: Joining again on a goal hosted elsewhere prints a "Give the role" command only the host can run, built from the ticket's role text
first.scenario: Ben's agent Juniper is a member of Ana's goal and does not hold `reviewer` (Ana took it, or Juniper was admitted without a role). Ben runs `locust --owner --agent claude-juniper-77aa0c52 goal join` with a ticket that carries role reviewer. Output: `claude-juniper-77aa0c52 is already in "Parser cleanup" as Juniper · auto.` then `Give the role: locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member 8d03f2b6 reviewer`. Ben runs it as printed and gets `denied: this goal is hosted on another computer; its host decides`.
first.evidence: only_you.rs:732-744 prints the line whenever the ticket's role is not held, with no check of `view.hosted_here`; the non-hosted caller is goal_join at only_you.rs:1024-1031 with `preview.role`. The daemon refuses every role change on a goal it does not host at node/access.rs:135-139. `goal add` cannot reach this (add_plan refuses non-hosted goals first), so only the join path is wrong. Fix record row 17 says the no-op output "gives a separate role command when applicable".
first.fix: Code should change: print the `role give` line only when `view.hosted_here`; otherwise say "The host gives roles." Add the non-hosted case to the already-member test.
first.person_sees: After a repeated join, Locust tells you to run a command that is then refused because only the host can run it.

second.statement: On a goal hosted on another computer, a repeated `goal join` for an agent that is already a member and does not hold the ticket's role prints `Give the role: locust --owner role give ...`, a command the daemon there always refuses because only the host's computer changes roles. The line is printed with no look at `view.hosted_here`; the hosted case is correct and is the only one tested.
second.scenario:
1. Ana hosts "Parser cleanup". Ben's agent Juniper is an admitted member on Ben's computer and does not hold `reviewer` (Ana ran `role take`, or Juniper was admitted with no role).
2. Ben runs `locust --owner --agent claude-juniper-77aa0c52 goal join --ticket-file T`, where T is any ticket for that goal that carries role `reviewer`. It can be the ticket he first joined with, even spent or expired: `goal_join` only parses and signature-checks it (`preview(now)` reports `expired` but does not fail) and returns before any daemon join call.
3. `join_plan` finds standing `member` (only_you.rs:969-974), so `goal_join` calls `already_member_output(..., preview.role.as_deref())` (only_you.rs:1023-1032).
4. `already_member_output` reads goal status, sees Juniper is not in `view.roles["reviewer"]`, and appends `Give the role: locust --owner role give --goal c01d55aa --member 8d03f2b6 reviewer` (only_you.rs:732-744). `view.hosted_here` is false and is never read.
5. Ben runs the printed command. The CLI (`roles::run`, roles.rs:170-222) sends `RoleGive`; `role_change` begins with `self.host(actor, &goal)?` (locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:345), which returns `denied: this goal is hosted on another computer; its host decides` (locust-core/src/node/access.rs:127-141).
The same line is printed when the agent itself runs `goal join` without `--owner` (same call site). `goal add` cannot reach it on a non-hosted goal: `add_plan` refuses at only_you.rs:772-777 first.
second.fix: Code should change, CLI only. In `already_member_output` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:702-750), when the role is not held, print the `role give` line only if `view.hosted_here`; otherwise append the plan's existing sentence "The host gives roles." (roles plan lines 564, 3305, 3548). This mirrors the fix already made for the missing-reviewers line in `presentation::goal_status` (presentation.rs:905-916). Extend the already-member test with a non-hosted case (the existing one, `confirmed_adds_carry_the_counting_role_and_repeats_keep_the_signed_name` in crates/locust/tests/t2_flow.rs:904-995, runs only on the hosting computer); the real member daemon set up in `a_real_member_daemon_reports_that_the_host_is_on_another_computer` (t2_flow.rs:998) is the natural place.
second.person_sees: After joining a goal a second time from a computer that does not host it, Locust says the agent is already in and suggests a "Give the role" command. Running that command fails with "this goal is hosted on another computer; its host decides". Nothing is changed or lost; the person is pointed at a step only the host can take.
second.reason:
I tried to break each step and none failed. Code at the cited lines is unchanged between 9c337df and HEAD (a4a5b55 is docs only).

- Reachable: `goal_join` (only_you.rs:1001-1032) has no hosted check before the early return; `member_name` and `join_plan` do not refuse an existing member; `Membership::Member` serializes to "member" (locust-proto/src/api.rs:1449-1456), so `plan.review["standing"] == "member"` is true on a member's computer.
- The line: only_you.rs:732-744 tests only whether the agent is among `view.roles[role]`. `hosted_here` is on the same `GoalStatus` (used at only_you.rs:772 in `add_plan`) but is not consulted here.
- The refusal: `Request::RoleGive` dispatches straight to `role_change` (requests/mod.rs:201-206), whose first statement is `self.host(...)` (goals.rs:345); access.rs:131-140 denies when this daemon does not hold the governance key. The CLI `roles::run` adds no earlier, friendlier refusal.
- No test pins the opposite: "is already in" appears only in t2_flow.rs:956 and :978, both on a single hosting participant; the join assertion there does not even check the role line.
- Not intended: the R4 review's proposed fix asked for the role line on `goal add` (host-only) and only the already-in sentence for `goal join` (research/v2-phase-r4-review-2026-10-06.md:668-669); fix record row 17 says "when applicable" (research/v2-phase-r4-fixes-2026-10-06.md:41). The same class of error (status telling a non-host reader to add or invite) was confirmed in R4 and fixed with a `hosted_here` branch and a comment saying the text "must not point the reader at a step it cannot take" (presentation.rs:905-907).

On the "ticket's role text" part of the title: the text is not dangerous. `Invitation::check` requires `is_role_name` (no control characters, organization.rs:295-297) and `quote_role` (roles.rs:112-122) single-quotes anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_-], so the printed command cannot be altered by the role text. The defect is only that the command cannot succeed on that computer. Low severity is right.

first.title: safe() still prints several invisible characters raw, though its comment says none can hide a difference between two names
first.scenario: Mallory joins as "Juniper" followed by U+17B4 (Khmer inherent vowel, a default-ignorable code point most fonts draw as nothing). Status lines print her as `"Juniper" (9f3b2c1d)`: chosen_name quotes the name because it is not plain ASCII, but safe leaves the hidden character in, so nothing on screen shows why the name is quoted or how it differs from the real `Juniper (8d03f2b6)`. Copying the quoted name into --member selects Mallory. Role names and task titles, which are never quoted this way, show no sign at all (two roles can both read `reviewer`).
first.evidence: level.rs:571-585 lists U+00AD, U+034F, U+061C, U+115F-1160, U+180B-180F, U+200B-200F, U+2028-202E, U+2060-206F, U+3164, U+FE00-FE0F, U+FEFF, U+FFA0, U+E0000-E0FFF. Unicode's Default_Ignorable_Code_Point also holds U+17B4-17B5, U+1BCA0-1BCA3, U+1D173-1D17A and U+FFF0-FFF8, which pass through. The doc comment at level.rs:564-566 promises that default-ignorable code points "that would hide a difference between two names" are escaped; the test at level.rs:1046-1050 checks five characters from the review's list only. is_member_name and is_role_name admit all of these.
first.fix: Code should change: add the four missing ranges to the match and to `terminal_controls_and_bidi_never_reach_the_terminal`.
first.person_sees: A member, role or task title can carry a hidden character that Locust promised to show as an escape, so two different names can look the same apart from a pair of quotes.

second.statement: `safe` (crates/locust-proto/src/api/level.rs:567) escapes most but not all of Unicode's default-ignorable code points: U+17B4-17B5, U+FFF0-FFF8, U+1BCA0-1BCA3 and U+1D173-1D17A print raw, so its doc comment (level.rs:564-566) overstates what it does. A hostile member can use one in their own name or a task title; role names are out of scope because only the host signs them.

first.title: A member prints with exactly eight key characters in the views, while the selector's refusal lengthens the prefix until members differ
first.scenario: A member generates keys until one shares its first eight hex characters with Harbor's key (about four billion tries, hours on one computer) and joins as `Harbor`. goal status then prints two lines `Member: Harbor (02020202) ...`, the Roles line lists `Harbor (02020202)` for either, and pending prints `Harbor (02020202): approve` under a result for a review the newcomer signed. Only `--member Harbor` tells them apart, by answering `Harbor (020202020a), Harbor (020202021c)`.
first.evidence: member_label_noting takes `&key.to_string()[..8]` (presentation.rs:261) and is the label of goal status members and roles, pending's Attempting and verdict lines, and the holders line of role give/take (roles.rs:285-290). Part B's selector labels use member_key_prefix (selectors.rs:118-131), which grows past eight until unique; its unit test asserts `Maple (0101010101)`. The same role give output therefore prints the member with eight characters in the `now:` line and with the longer prefix in the `Undo:` line. The plan asks for eight characters (roles plan line 2738), so the plan changes with the code.
first.fix: Have member_label_noting print `selectors::member_key_prefix(members, key)` in place of the fixed eight characters, and change the plan's `first eight characters of its key` to the shortest unique prefix of at least eight.
first.person_sees: Normally nothing. A determined member can make its line in goal status, in the roles list and under a review read exactly like another member's, key included.

second.statement: member_label_noting cuts every member key to a fixed eight hex characters, so a member who makes a key sharing those eight characters with another member's and joins under the same name prints with an identical label in the Roles line of goal status, in pending's Attempting and verdict lines and in the holders line of role give/take, while the selector refusal and the Undo line lengthen the prefix until the two differ. The code does what the plan asks (plan line 2738), so this is a gap in the plan that the code inherits, not a departure by the builder.
second.scenario: 1. A member holding a ticket searches for a key whose first eight hex characters equal an existing member's (keys print as lowercase hex, so this is 32 bits, about four billion tries; any member's prefix will do as the target). 2. It joins with that member's name. plan_join admits it unattended: it checks only that the key is not already a member and never compares names or key prefixes. 3. goal status then prints `Roles: reviewer Harbor (02020202), Harbor (02020202)` and the `Host:` line `Harbor (02020202)`; pending prints `  Harbor (02020202): approve (EVENT)` for a review the newcomer signed and `Attempting: Harbor (02020202)`; role give prints both holders with the same eight characters in the `now:` line and the longer, distinct prefix in the `Undo:` line of the same output. 4. Corrections to the report: the two `Member:` lines are not identical as they stand. Each also carries `local` or `remote` and eight characters of the member's endpoint, so on the host's computer its own agent reads `local` and the newcomer `remote`, and elsewhere they differ by endpoint unless the newcomer also searches for a matching endpoint key (a second, separate search). In role give the host's agent is marked `the host's agent`. And `--member Harbor` is not the only thing that tells them apart: `--member 02020202` gets the same refusal with the longer prefixes. No command acts on the wrong member and approvals are counted by key, so the count stays right; the harm is a person reading a role or a verdict as another member's.
second.fix: Change plan and code together. In member_label_noting (crates/locust/src/cli/presentation.rs:261) replace `&key.to_string()[..8]` with `super::selectors::member_key_prefix(members, key)`; every caller already passes the goal's member list, the function is visible to sibling modules, and the existing test (`Maple (01010101)`, one member) still holds. Reword plan line 2738 and the mockup note at line 469 of docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md from "the first eight characters of its key" to the shortest prefix of at least eight characters that no other member's key starts with, and add a label test with two members sharing eight characters. Same class, worth the same substitution while there: the `member remove` plan and result print the bare key cut to eight (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:1305 and :1348).
second.person_sees: Normally nothing changes. If a member goes to the trouble of making a look-alike key and joining under someone else's name, the roles list and the line under a review show two entries that read exactly the same, name and key, so a person cannot tell from those lines who holds the role or who approved. The member list still differs by the computer shown beside each one, and any command that names the member stops and shows longer keys that do differ.
second.reason: Read, not run. presentation.rs:260-272 takes `&key.to_string()[..8]`; keys display as hex (locust-proto/src/id.rs:96-100), so eight characters are 32 bits. Callers: Host line (presentation.rs:287), Attempting (440), verdict lines (520), Member lines (850), Roles line (887), role give/take holders (roles.rs:285-290). selectors.rs:118-131 grows the prefix from 8 to 64 until unique and its test says so ("Candidate labels expand beyond eight characters when needed", selectors.rs:414-421); roles.rs:123-133 uses it for the Undo line, so one role give output mixes both. Nothing pins the opposite: the label test at presentation.rs:1517-1531 has one member.
